translations.literal: At the year's festivals he collects living people's gall and puts it in wine to drink with his family, and also uses it to bathe his body, saying "my whole body is gall."
translations.idiomatic: At the seasonal rites he collects the gall bladders of living people, mixes them into wine to drink with his family, and bathes in them as well, declaring, "My whole body is gall."

sentences.zh: 其國人采以獻王，又以洗象目。

translations.literal: The people of the country gather it as tribute to the king, and also use it to wash elephants' eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The people gather gall for presentation to the king and also use it to wash elephants' eyes.

sentences.zh: 每伺人於道，出不意急殺之，取膽以去。

translations.literal: They often lie in wait on the roads and suddenly kill passers-by without warning, taking the gall and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: They often ambush travelers on the road, killing them without warning to extract the gall and flee.

sentences.zh: 若其人驚覺，則膽已先裂，不足用矣。

translations.literal: If the victim becomes startled and wakes, the gall has already burst and is useless.
translations.idiomatic: If the victim wakes in alarm, the gall bladder has already ruptured and is worthless.

sentences.zh: 置眾膽於器，華人膽輒居上，故尤貴之。

translations.literal: When many gall bladders are placed in a vessel, the bile of Chinese people always rises to the top, and for this reason it is especially prized.
translations.idiomatic: When many gall bladders are collected in a vessel, the bile of Chinese people always floats to the top, which is why it is especially prized.

sentences.zh: 五 六月間，商人出，必戒備。

translations.literal: Between the fifth and sixth months merchants who go out must take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: During the fifth and sixth months, merchants who venture abroad must stay on guard.

sentences.zh: 王在位三十年，則避位入深山，以兄弟子侄代，而己持 齋受戒，告於天曰：「我為君無道，願狼虎食我，或病死。

translations.literal: After the king has reigned thirty years, he abdicates and withdraws deep into the mountains, letting brothers, sons, and nephews take his place, while he himself keeps vegetarian fasts and receives precepts, praying to heaven: "I have ruled without the Way; may wolves and tigers devour me, or may I die of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty years on the throne the king abdicates and retreats deep into the mountains, leaving a brother, son, or nephew to rule in his place. He then keeps a vegetarian fast, takes Buddhist vows, and prays to heaven: "I have ruled without virtue. May wolves and tigers devour me, or may I die of sickness."

sentences.zh: 」居一年無恙，則復位 如初。

translations.literal: " If after living there a year he remains unharmed, then he shall resume the throne as before.
translations.idiomatic: If he survives a full year unharmed, he returns to the throne as before.

sentences.zh: 國中呼為「昔嚟馬哈剌」，乃至尊至聖之稱也。

translations.literal: In the country this is called "Xilai Mahala," the title of supreme honor and sanctity.
translations.idiomatic: Within the kingdom this rite is known as Silaimahar—the title of the highest and most sacred honor.

sentences.zh: 國不甚富，惟犀象最多。

translations.literal: The country is not very wealthy; rhinoceroses and elephants are its most plentiful resources.
translations.idiomatic: The country is not especially rich, but rhinoceroses and elephants are more abundant there than anywhere else.

sentences.zh: 烏木、降香，樵以為薪。

translations.literal: Ebony and agarwood are cut for firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Ebony and eaglewood are chopped up and burned as fuel.

sentences.zh: 棋柟香獨產其地一山，酋長 遣人守之，民不得采，犯者至斷手。

translations.literal: Kyara aloeswood is found on only one mountain in the region; the chieftain posts guards over it, and the people may not gather it—offenders face amputation of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Kyara aloeswood grows on a single mountain in the realm. The chieftain posts guards there, and commoners are forbidden to harvest it; violators may have their hands cut off.

sentences.zh: 有鱷魚潭，獄疑不決者，令兩造騎牛過其旁，曲者，魚輒躍而食之，直者，即 數往返，不食也。

translations.literal: There is a crocodile pond; when a legal case cannot be resolved, both parties are made to ride oxen past it—the guilty party is leapt upon and eaten by the crocodile, while the innocent may pass back and forth several times without being eaten.
translations.idiomatic: There is a crocodile pool. When a lawsuit cannot be decided, both sides are made to ride oxen past it. The guilty man's crocodile leaps out and devours him; the innocent man may pass back and forth repeatedly without being touched.

sentences.zh: 有屍頭蠻者，一名屍致魚，本婦人，惟無瞳神為異。

translations.literal: There are "corpse-head barbarians," also called corpse-headed fish-demons; they were originally women, distinguished only by the absence of pupils in their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: There are flying-head demons, also called corpse-headed fish-spirits. They are women, distinguishable only by the lack of pupils in their eyes.

sentences.zh: 夜中與人同 寢，忽飛頭食人穢物，來即復活。

translations.literal: At night they sleep with others, but suddenly their heads fly off to feed on human filth, then return and the body lives again.
translations.idiomatic: At night they sleep beside others, but their heads suddenly detach and fly off to consume human filth before returning to the body, which then lives again.

sentences.zh: 若人知而封其頸，或移之他所，其婦即死。

translations.literal: If someone discovers this and seals the neck, or moves the head elsewhere, the woman dies.
translations.idiomatic: If someone discovers what is happening and seals the neck, or moves the head elsewhere, the woman dies.

sentences.zh: 國設 厲禁，有而不告者，罪及一家。

translations.literal: The state has strict prohibitions; anyone who knows of such a person and does not report it brings punishment upon the whole household.
translations.idiomatic: The state maintains severe laws on the matter. Anyone who knows of such a creature and fails to report it brings punishment on the entire household.

sentences.zh: 賓童龍

translations.literal: Panduranga
translations.idiomatic: Panduranga

sentences.zh: 賓童龍國，與占城接壤。

translations.literal: The kingdom of Panduranga borders Champa.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Panduranga lay on Champa's border.

sentences.zh: 或言如來入舍衛國乞食，即其地。

translations.literal: Some say it was the place where the Tathagata entered Shravasti to beg for alms.
translations.idiomatic: Some say it was the very place where the Buddha entered Shravasti to beg for food.

sentences.zh: 氣候、草木、人物、 風土，大類占城，惟遭喪能持服，葬以僻地，設齋禮佛，婚姻偶合。

translations.literal: Climate, vegetation, people, and customs greatly resemble Champa, except that they observe mourning dress, bury the dead in secluded places, hold Buddhist feasts, and marriages are formed by mutual pairing.
translations.idiomatic: Its climate, flora, people, and customs closely resemble Champa's, except that the people observe mourning dress, bury the dead in remote places, hold Buddhist feasts, and marry by mutual consent.

sentences.zh: 酋出入乘象或 馬，從者百餘人，前後贊唱。

translations.literal: The chieftain goes out riding an elephant or horse, attended by more than a hundred followers who chant praise before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain travels by elephant or horse, accompanied by more than a hundred retainers who sing his praises fore and aft.

sentences.zh: 民編茅覆屋。

translations.literal: The people weave rushes to roof their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: The people weave rushes into roofs for their houses.

sentences.zh: 貨用金、銀、花布。

translations.literal: For commerce they use gold, silver, and patterned cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, and patterned cloth serve as currency.

sentences.zh: 有崑崙山，節然大海中，與占城及東、西竺鼎峙相望。

translations.literal: There is Kunlun Mountain, rising abruptly from the great sea, standing in triangular opposition with Champa and East and West India across the waters.
translations.idiomatic: Kunlun Mountain rises sheer from the open ocean, standing like a tripod with Champa and the lands of East and West India facing one another across the sea.

sentences.zh: 其山方廣而高，其海即 曰崑崙洋。

translations.literal: The mountain is broad, square, and lofty, and the sea there is called the Kunlun Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain is broad, high, and imposing, and the surrounding sea is known as the Kunlun Ocean.

sentences.zh: 諸往西洋者，必待順風，七晝夜始得過，故舟人為之諺曰：「上怕七州， 下怕崑崙，針迷舵失，人船莫存。

translations.literal: All who sail to the Western Ocean must wait for a fair wind and need seven days and nights to pass it, so sailors have a saying: "Above one fears the Seven Isles, below one fears Kunlun; lose needle and rudder, and neither man nor ship survives."
translations.idiomatic: Every ship bound for the Western Ocean must wait for a favorable wind and needs seven days and nights to clear it. Sailors therefore have a proverb: "Fear the Seven Isles above, fear Kunlun below; lose your compass and rudder, and neither crew nor vessel will survive."

sentences.zh: 」此山無異產。

translations.literal: This mountain yields no unusual products.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain produces nothing of note.

sentences.zh: 人皆穴居巢處，食果實魚蝦，無室廬井灶。

translations.literal: The people all live in caves and nests, eating fruit, fish, and shrimp; they have no houses, storehouses, wells, or hearths.
translations.idiomatic: Its inhabitants live in caves and treetop shelters, eating fruit, fish, and shrimp. They have no buildings, granaries, wells, or cooking hearths.

sentences.zh: 真臘，在占城南，順風三晝夜可至。

translations.literal: Zhenla lies south of Champa; with a fair wind one can reach it in three days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenla lay south of Champa. With a fair wind the voyage took three days and nights.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐及宋皆朝貢。

translations.literal: Under the Sui, Tang, and Song it sent tribute to the court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui, Tang, and Song dynasties it paid tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 宋慶元中，滅占城而 並其地，因改國名曰占臘。

translations.literal: In the Qingyuan reign of the Song it destroyed Champa and annexed its territory, and therefore changed its name to Zhanla.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingyuan era of the Song it conquered Champa and absorbed its territory, renaming the realm Zhanla.

sentences.zh: 元時仍稱真臘。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan it was again called Zhenla.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it reverted to the name Zhenla.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，遣使臣郭徵等齎詔撫諭其國。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 3 envoys including Guo Zheng were sent bearing an edict to comfort and instruct the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 the envoy Guo Zheng and others were dispatched with an edict to reassure and instruct the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 四年，其國巴山王忽爾那遣使進表， 貢方物，賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year King Huer-na of Bashan sent envoys with a memorial, tribute goods, and congratulations for the coming New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year King Huer-na of Bashan sent envoys with a memorial, local products, and New Year's greetings for the coming year.

sentences.zh: 詔賜《大統歷》及彩幣，使者亦給賜有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted the Datong Calendar and colored silks, and the envoys also received graded gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the Datong Calendar and colored silks, and the envoys received gifts scaled to their rank.

sentences.zh: 六年進貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year it sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year it sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十二 年，王參答甘武者持達志遣使來貢，宴賜如前。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year King Candramauli, ruler of the realm, sent envoys with tribute; feasting and gifts followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year King Candramauli, lord of the realm, sent tribute envoys, who were feasted and rewarded as before.

sentences.zh: 十三年復貢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year it sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year it sent tribute once more.

sentences.zh: 十六年遣使齎勘合文 冊賜其王。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year envoys were sent bearing tally documents and patent to invest the king.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year envoys were dispatched with tally documents and letters patent for the king.

sentences.zh: 凡國中使至，勘合不符者，即屬矯偽，許縶縛以聞。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys from the kingdom arrived, if their tally did not match it was deemed fraudulent and they were permitted to be bound and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys from the kingdom arrived, a mismatch in the tally was treated as forgery, and they could be seized and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 復遣使賜織金文綺 三十二、磁器萬九千。

translations.literal: Envoys were again sent to grant thirty-two bolts of brocaded silk with woven gold patterns and nineteen thousand pieces of porcelain.
translations.idiomatic: Further envoys were sent bearing thirty-two bolts of brocaded silk with woven gold patterns and nineteen thousand pieces of porcelain.

sentences.zh: 其王遣使來貢。

translations.literal: The king sent tribute envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The king dispatched tribute envoys in return.

sentences.zh: 十九年遣行人劉敏、唐敬偕中官齎磁器往賜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the court courier Liu Min and Tang Jing, together with eunuchs, were sent bearing porcelain as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the courier Liu Min and Tang Jing, accompanied by eunuchs, were sent with porcelain gifts.

sentences.zh: 明年，敬等還，王遣使貢象五十九、香六萬斤。

translations.literal: The following year, after Jing and the others returned, the king sent envoys presenting fifty-nine elephants and sixty thousand jin of incense.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after Tang Jing's party returned, the king sent envoys with fifty-nine elephants and sixty thousand jin of incense.

sentences.zh: 尋遣使賜其王鍍金銀印，王及妃皆 有賜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward envoys were sent to grant the king a gilded silver seal; both the king and the consort received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the court sent envoys to bestow a gilded silver seal on the king, with gifts for both the king and the queen.

sentences.zh: 其王參烈實{田比}邪甘菩者遣使貢象及方物。

translations.literal: King Samleat Piyekampol sent envoys with elephants and local products.
translations.idiomatic: King Samleat Piyekampol sent envoys bearing elephants and local products.

sentences.zh: 明年復貢像二十八、象奴三十 四人、番奴四十五人，謝賜印之恩。

translations.literal: The next year tribute came again: twenty-eight elephant images, thirty-four elephant keepers, and forty-five foreign servants, in thanks for the gift of the seal.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent tribute again: twenty-eight elephant images, thirty-four elephant handlers, and forty-five foreign attendants, in gratitude for the seal.

sentences.zh: 二十二年三貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year it sent tribute three times.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year it sent tribute three times.

sentences.zh: 明年復貢。

translations.literal: The following year it sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that it sent tribute once more.

sentences.zh: 其國城隍周七十餘里，幅員廣數千里。

translations.literal: The kingdom's walled city is more than seventy li in circumference, and its territory extends several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's walls ran more than seventy li around, and the realm stretched several thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 國中有金塔、金橋、殿宇三十餘所。

translations.literal: Within the kingdom are more than thirty gold towers, gold bridges, and halls.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty gold pagodas, gold bridges, and palace halls stood within the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 王 歲時一會，羅列玉猿、孔雀、白象、犀牛於前，名曰百塔洲。

translations.literal: Once a year the king holds a gathering, arraying jade monkeys, peacocks, white elephants, and rhinoceroses before him—a place called Hundred-Tower Reach.
translations.idiomatic: Once a year the king held a great assembly, displaying jade monkeys, peacocks, white elephants, and rhinoceroses before him at a place called Hundred-Pagoda Reach.

sentences.zh: 盛食以金盤、金椀， 故有「富貴真臘」之諺。

translations.literal: Food is served in gold platters and gold bowls, hence the proverb "wealthy and noble Zhenla."
translations.idiomatic: Meals were served on gold platters and in gold bowls, giving rise to the saying "rich and noble Zhenla."

sentences.zh: 民俗富饒。

translations.literal: Customs and people are prosperous and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The people were prosperous and well provided for.

sentences.zh: 天時常熱，不識霜雪，禾一歲數稔。

translations.literal: The climate is always hot; frost and snow are unknown, and grain ripens several times in one year.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was perpetually warm. Frost and snow were unknown, and grain could be harvested several times a year.

sentences.zh: 男女椎結， 穿短衫，圍梢布。

translations.literal: Men and women wear topknots, short jackets, and wrap themselves in sarongs.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women alike wore topknots, short jackets, and sarongs wrapped around the waist.

sentences.zh: 刑有劓、刖、刺配，盜則去手足。

translations.literal: Punishments include nose-cutting, foot-cutting, and tattooing for exile; thieves have hands and feet removed.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties included cutting off the nose, cutting off the feet, and tattooing for banishment; thieves had their hands and feet removed.

sentences.zh: 番人殺唐人罪死；

translations.literal: If a foreigner kills a Chinese person, the penalty is death;
translations.idiomatic: If a native killed a Chinese person, the penalty was death;

sentences.zh: 唐人殺番人 則罰金，無金則鬻身贖罪。

translations.literal: if a Chinese person kills a foreigner, a fine is imposed, and if he has no gold he sells himself into servitude to redeem the offense.
translations.idiomatic: if a Chinese person killed a native, he paid a fine, and if he had no gold he sold himself into bondage to atone for the crime.

sentences.zh: 唐人者，諸番呼華人之稱也，凡海外諸國盡然。

translations.literal: "Tang person" is what all the foreign peoples call Chinese; this is so in every overseas country.
translations.idiomatic: "Tang person" was the name all foreign peoples used for Chinese, and the usage was the same in every overseas country.

sentences.zh: 婚嫁， 兩傢俱八日不出門，晝夜燃燈。

translations.literal: At marriage, both families remain indoors for eight days without going out, keeping lamps burning day and night.
translations.idiomatic: At a wedding both families stayed indoors for eight days without venturing out, keeping lamps lit around the clock.

sentences.zh: 人死置於野，任烏鳶食，俄頃食盡者，謂為福報。

translations.literal: When someone dies the body is placed in the open and left for vultures and kites to eat; if it is consumed quickly, this is called blessed reward.
translations.idiomatic: When a person died the body was left in the open for vultures and kites to devour. If it was eaten quickly, that was considered a blessed karmic reward.

sentences.zh: 居喪，但髡其發，女子則額上剪髮如錢大，曰用此報親。

translations.literal: In mourning, only the hair is shaved; women clip a coin-sized patch of hair on the forehead, saying they repay their parents thus.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning the hair was shaved; women clipped a coin-sized tuft from the forehead, saying this was how they repaid their parents.

sentences.zh: 文字以麂鹿雜皮染黑，用 粉為小條畫於上，永不脫落。

translations.literal: Writing is done on deerskin and mixed pelts dyed black, with powder applied in thin lines on the surface, which never rub off.
translations.idiomatic: Writing was done on deerskin and other hides dyed black, with powdered ink drawn in fine strokes on the surface so that it never faded.

sentences.zh: 以十月為歲首，閏悉用九月。

translations.literal: The tenth month is taken as the year's beginning; intercalary months are all placed in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth month marked the start of the year, and any intercalary month was inserted in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 夜分四更。

translations.literal: Night is divided into four watches.
translations.idiomatic: The night was divided into four watches.

sentences.zh: 亦有曉天文 者，能算日月薄蝕。

translations.literal: Some also know astronomy and can calculate solar and lunar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Some men understood astronomy and could calculate solar and lunar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 其地謂儒為班詰，僧為苧姑，道為八思。

translations.literal: In that land Confucians are called banzhuo, monks are called zhugu, and Daoists are called basi.
translations.idiomatic: In that country Confucian scholars were called banzhuo, Buddhist monks zhugu, and Daoist priests basi.

sentences.zh: 班詰不知讀何書，由 此入仕者為華貫。

translations.literal: Banzhuo do not know what books they study; those who enter office through this path form the civil elite.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew what texts the banzhuo read, but those who entered government by this route formed the educated elite.

sentences.zh: 先時項掛一白線以自別，既貴曳白如故。

translations.literal: Formerly they hung a white thread on the neck to distinguish themselves; after rising high in rank they still drag the white thread as before.
translations.idiomatic: They once wore a white cord around the neck to mark their status, and even after attaining high office they continued to trail the white cord as before.

sentences.zh: 俗尚釋教，僧皆食魚、 肉，或以供佛，惟不飲酒。

translations.literal: The custom esteems Buddhism; monks all eat fish and meat, sometimes offering them to the Buddha, but they do not drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism was widely honored. Monks ate fish and meat, sometimes offering them to the Buddha, but they abstained from wine.

sentences.zh: 其國自稱甘孛智，後訛為甘破蔗，萬曆後又改為柬埔寨。

translations.literal: The kingdom calls itself Camboja; this later became corrupted to Ganpozhe, and after the Wanli reign was changed again to Cambodia.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom called itself Camboja, which later corrupted to Ganpozhe and, after the Wanli reign, was rendered as Cambodia.

sentences.zh: 暹羅，在占城西南，順風十晝夜可至，即隋、唐赤土國。

translations.literal: Siam lies southwest of Champa; with a fair wind it can be reached in ten days and nights. It is the Chitu kingdom of the Sui and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Siam lay southwest of Champa. With a fair wind the voyage took ten days and nights. It was the Chitu kingdom of Sui and Tang times.

sentences.zh: 後分為羅斛、暹二國。

translations.literal: Later it split into two states, Luo-hu and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Later it divided into two kingdoms, Luo-hu and Siam proper.

sentences.zh: 暹土瘠不宜稼，羅斛地平衍，種多獲，暹仰給焉。

translations.literal: The land of Xian was barren and unsuitable for crops; the land of Luo Hu was level and expansive, and when planted yielded abundantly; Xian relied on it for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Siam proper had poor soil ill suited to farming, while Luo Hu's land was flat and fertile and produced bountiful harvests; Siam depended on Luo Hu for its grain.

sentences.zh: 元時，暹常入貢。

translations.literal: In Yuan times, Xian frequently sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuan dynasty, Xian regularly sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 其後，羅斛強， 並有暹地，遂稱暹羅斛國。

translations.literal: Afterward Luo Hu grew strong, annexed Xian's territory, and thus was called the state of Xian-Luo Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Luo Hu grew powerful, absorbed Siam, and the united realm came to be called Xian-Luo Hu.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，命使臣呂宗俊等齎詔諭其國。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 3, [the emperor] ordered envoys such as Lü Zongjun to carry an edict and notify that country.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu, the emperor sent envoys led by Lü Zongjun bearing an imperial edict to notify the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 四年，其王參烈昭{田比}牙遣使奉表， 與宗俊等偕來，貢馴象、六足龜及方物，詔賜其王錦綺及使者幣帛有差。

translations.literal: In year 4, its king Cansilie Zha Bi Ya dispatched envoys presenting a memorial, coming together with Zongjun and others, offering tribute of tame elephants, six-legged tortoises, and local products; an edict bestowed upon the king brocades and silks and upon the envoys silks in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, King Cansilie Zha Bi Ya sent envoys with a formal memorial, arriving together with Zongjun's mission bearing tame elephants, six-legged tortoises, and other tribute goods. An imperial edict awarded the king brocades and silks and granted the envoys gifts in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 已，復遣 使賀明年正旦，詔賜《大統歷》及彩幣。

translations.literal: Soon after, [he] again sent envoys to congratulate the coming New Year's Day, and an edict granted the Datong Calendar and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he sent envoys again to offer New Year's greetings for the coming year, and the court bestowed the Datong Calendar and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 五年貢黑熊、白猿及方物。

translations.literal: In year 5 [they] offered tribute of black bears, white gibbons, and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year they sent tribute of black bears, white gibbons, and other local products.

sentences.zh: 明年復來貢。

translations.literal: The next year they again came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 其王之姊參烈思寧別遣使進金葉表，貢方物於中宮，卻之。

translations.literal: The king's elder sister Cansilie Si Ning separately sent envoys presenting a gold-leaf memorial, offering tribute goods to the inner palace; [the emperor] declined them.
translations.idiomatic: The king's elder sister Cansilie Si Ning separately dispatched envoys with a gold-leaf memorial and tribute for the empress; the emperor refused the gifts.

sentences.zh: 已而其姊復遣使來貢， 帝仍卻之，而宴賚其使。

translations.literal: Soon after the elder sister again sent envoys with tribute; the emperor still declined them, but feasted and rewarded the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the elder sister sent envoys with tribute again; the emperor once more declined the gifts but hosted and rewarded the mission.

sentences.zh: 時其王懦而不武，國人推其伯父參烈寶{田比}邪思裡 哆囉祿主國事，遣使來告，貢方物，宴賚如制。

translations.literal: At that time the king was weak and not martial; the people of the country promoted his uncle Cansilie Bao Bi Ye Siliduoluo to manage state affairs, and he sent envoys to report this, offering tribute goods; feasting and rewards followed the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The king was timid and unwarlike, so his subjects installed his uncle Cansilie Bao Bi Ye Siliduoluo to govern. He sent envoys to inform the court and presented tribute, and they were feasted and rewarded according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 已而新王遣使來貢、謝恩，其使者 亦有獻，帝不納。

translations.literal: Soon the new king sent envoys with tribute and to express gratitude; the envoys also had gifts to present, but the emperor did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: The new king soon sent envoys with tribute and thanks; they brought additional offerings as well, but the emperor declined to accept them.

sentences.zh: 已，遣使賀明年正旦，貢方物，且獻本國地圖。

translations.literal: Soon afterward [he] sent envoys to congratulate the coming New Year's Day, offering tribute goods and also presenting a map of his country.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to greet the coming New Year, bringing tribute and a map of his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 七年，使臣沙裡拔來貢。

translations.literal: In year 7, the envoy Sha Liba came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the envoy Sha Liba arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 言去年舟次烏豬洋，遭風壞舟，飄至海南，賴官司救 護，尚存飄余兜羅綿、降香、蘇木諸物進獻，廣東省臣以聞。

translations.literal: He said that last year his ship had stopped at Wuzhu Shoals, encountered a storm that wrecked the vessel, and drifted to Hainan; relying on official rescue and care, they still had salvaged douluo cotton, agarwood, sappan wood, and other items to present; the Guangdong provincial officials reported this.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that the previous year his ship had anchored at Black Pig Shoal when a storm wrecked it and drove them to Hainan. Official aid had saved them, and they still had salvaged douluo cotton, agarwood, sappan wood, and other goods to offer. The Guangdong provincial officials reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝怪其無表，既言舟 覆，而方物乃有存者，疑其為番商，命卻之。

translations.literal: The emperor found it strange that they had no memorial; since they said the ship had capsized yet local products remained, he suspected them of being foreign merchants and ordered the goods refused.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought it odd that they brought no formal memorial. If their ship had been wrecked, he reasoned, how could tribute goods still survive? Suspecting them of being foreign merchants, he ordered the offerings turned away.

sentences.zh: 諭中書及禮部臣曰：「古諸侯於天子， 比年一小聘，三年一大聘。

translations.literal: He instructed the Secretariat and Ministry of Rites officials, saying: "In antiquity feudal lords toward the Son of Heaven paid a minor visit every other year and a major visit every three years.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed officials of the Secretariat and the Ministry of Rites: "In antiquity, feudal lords paid the Son of Heaven a minor visit every other year and a major visit every three years.

sentences.zh: 九州之外，則每世一朝，所貢方物，表誠敬而已。

translations.literal: Beyond the Nine Provinces, each generation came to court once; the local products offered were merely to express sincerity and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Nine Provinces, each generation came to court only once, and the goods they offered merely expressed sincerity and respect.

sentences.zh: 惟高 麗頗知禮樂，故令三年一貢。

translations.literal: Only Goryeo was well versed in ritual and music, so it was permitted tribute once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Only Goryeo, being well versed in ritual and music, was allowed to send tribute once every three years.

sentences.zh: 他遠國，如占城、安南、西洋瑣裡、爪哇、浡泥、三 佛齊、暹羅斛、真臘諸國，入貢既頻，勞費太甚。

translations.literal: Other distant countries, such as Champa, Annam, Saoli of the Western Ocean, Java, Poni, Srivijaya, Xian-Luo Hu, and Khmer, coming with tribute so frequently, caused excessive labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Other distant kingdoms—Champa, Annam, Saoli of the Western Ocean, Java, Poni, Srivijaya, Xian-Luo Hu, and Khmer—were sending tribute so often that the burden and expense had become excessive.

sentences.zh: 今不必復爾，其移牒諸國俾知之。

translations.literal: Now there is no need to continue thus; send notices to the various countries so they may know.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to continue this way; send notices to all the kingdoms so they will understand.

sentences.zh: 」 然而來者不止。

translations.literal: " Nevertheless, those who came did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: " Nevertheless, tributary missions kept arriving anyway.

sentences.zh: 其世子蘇門邦王昭祿群膺亦遣使上箋於皇太子，貢方物。

translations.literal: Its crown prince, King Zhao Lu Qun Ying of Sumenbangg, also sent envoys presenting a petition to the crown prince, offering tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, King Zhao Lu Qun Ying of Sumenbangg, also sent envoys with a petition to the crown prince and tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 命引其使 朝東宮，宴賚遣之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] ordered that the envoys be led to audience at the Eastern Palace, feasted, rewarded, and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the envoys brought before the crown prince, then feasted, rewarded, and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 八年再入貢。

translations.literal: In year 8 they again came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 其舊明台王世子昭孛羅局亦遣使奉表朝貢，宴賚 如王使。

translations.literal: The former Mingtai King's crown prince Zhao Bo Luo Ju also sent envoys presenting a memorial and tribute, and feasting and rewards were the same as for the king's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The former Mingtai king's heir, Zhao Bo Luo Ju, also sent envoys with a memorial and tribute, and they were feasted and rewarded on the same terms as the king's mission.

sentences.zh: 十年，昭祿群膺承其父命來朝。

translations.literal: In year 10, Zhao Lu Qun Ying, at his father's command, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zhao Lu Qun Ying came to court on his father's orders.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，命禮部員外郎王恆等齎詔及印賜之，文 曰「暹羅國王之印」，並賜世子衣幣及道里費。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered Wang Heng, assistant department director of the Ministry of Rites, and others to carry an edict and seal to bestow upon him, reading "Seal of the King of Siam," and also bestowed upon the crown prince robes, silks, and travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor sent Wang Heng, an assistant director in the Ministry of Rites, and others with an edict and a seal inscribed "Seal of the King of Siam," along with robes, silks, and travel expenses for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 自是，其國遵朝命，始稱暹羅；

translations.literal: From this time, the country obeyed the court's command and first took the name Siam;
translations.idiomatic: From then on, following the court's directive, the kingdom came to be called Siam;

sentences.zh: 比 年一貢，或一年兩貢。

translations.literal: tribute once every other year, or twice in one year.
translations.idiomatic: sending tribute every other year, or sometimes twice in a single year.

sentences.zh: 至正統後，或數年一貢雲。

translations.literal: After the Zhengtong reign, sometimes tribute once every several years, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengtong reign, missions reportedly came only once every few years.

sentences.zh: 十六年，賜勘合文冊及文綺、磁器，與真臘等。

translations.literal: In year 16, [the court] bestowed tally documents and registers, patterned silks, and porcelain, the same as for Khmer and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the court granted tally registers, patterned silks, and porcelain—the same treatment as Khmer and the other kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 二十年貢胡椒一萬斤、蘇木一 萬斤。

translations.literal: In year 20 they offered tribute of ten thousand jin of pepper and ten thousand jin of sappan wood.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year they sent ten thousand jin of pepper and ten thousand jin of sappan wood as tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝遣官厚報之。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched officials to reward them generously in return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent officials to return the favor with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 時溫州民有市其沉香諸物者，所司坐以通番，當棄市。

translations.literal: At that time Wenzhou commoners who traded for their agarwood and other goods were charged by the authorities with illicit foreign trade and sentenced to death by public execution.
translations.idiomatic: Some Wenzhou merchants who bought their agarwood and other goods were charged with illegal overseas trade and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 帝曰： 「溫州乃暹羅必經之地，因其往來而市之，非通番也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wenzhou is a place Siam must pass through on its journeys; trading with them because of their coming and going is not illicit foreign trade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wenzhou lies on Siam's regular route of travel; trading with them as they come and go is not illicit foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 」乃獲宥。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 二十一，年貢象 三十、番奴六十。

translations.literal: In year 21 they offered tribute of thirty elephants and sixty foreign slaves.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year they sent thirty elephants and sixty foreign slaves as tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，世子昭祿群膺遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In year 22, Crown Prince Zhao Lu Qun Ying dispatched envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Crown Prince Zhao Lu Qun Ying sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十三，年貢蘇木、胡椒、 降香十七萬斤。

translations.literal: In year 23 they offered tribute of sappan wood, pepper, and agarwood totaling one hundred seventy thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year they sent one hundred seventy thousand jin of sappan wood, pepper, and agarwood combined.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，昭祿群膺遣使朝貢，且告父喪。

translations.literal: In year 28, Zhao Lu Qun Ying sent envoys to court with tribute and to report his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year Zhao Lu Qun Ying sent envoys with tribute and news of his father's death.

sentences.zh: 命中官趙達等往祭，敕世子嗣王位， 賜賚有加。

translations.literal: [The emperor] ordered eunuch officials Zhao Da and others to go perform sacrifices, commanded the crown prince to succeed to the kingship, and granted rewards with added generosity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuch Zhao Da and others to conduct the funeral rites, confirmed the crown prince as king, and awarded him especially generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「朕自即位以來，命使出疆，周於四維，足履其境者三十六，聲 聞於耳者三十一，風殊俗異。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Since I ascended the throne, I have sent envoys beyond the borders throughout the four quarters; thirty-six lands have been trodden by foot, thirty-one heard of by name—all with different customs and manners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Since I ascended the throne, I have sent envoys throughout the four quarters; I have set foot in thirty-six lands and heard of thirty-one more, each with its own customs and ways.

sentences.zh: 大國十有八，小國百四十九，較之於今，暹羅最近。

translations.literal: Great states number eighteen, small states one hundred forty-nine; compared with these of today, Siam is nearest.
translations.idiomatic: There are eighteen great states and one hundred forty-nine small ones; among them all, Siam is the nearest to us today.

sentences.zh: 邇者使至，知爾先王已逝。

translations.literal: Recently your envoys arrived, and I learned that your late king has passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Your envoys have just arrived with word that your late king has passed away.

sentences.zh: 王紹先三之緒，有道於邦家，臣民懽懌。

translations.literal: The king inherits the legacy of his three predecessors, has the Way in his state and household, and officials and people are rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: You inherit the line of your three royal forebears, govern the realm with virtue, and your officials and people are glad at heart.

sentences.zh: 茲特遣人錫命， 王其罔失法度，罔淫於樂，以光前烈。

translations.literal: Now I specially send persons to bestow the mandate; the king should not lose the laws and standards, should not indulge in pleasure, so as to glorify the former achievements.
translations.idiomatic: I now send envoys to confer imperial investiture upon you. Do not abandon the laws, and do not abandon yourself to pleasure, so that you may honor your ancestors' achievements.

sentences.zh: 欽哉。

translations.literal: Respect this!
translations.idiomatic: Take heed!

sentences.zh: 」成祖即位，詔諭其國。

translations.literal: " When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he issued an edict notifying that country.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Yongle Emperor came to the throne, he sent an edict to notify the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年賜 其王昭祿群膺哆囉諦剌駝紐鍍金銀印，其王即遣使謝恩。

translations.literal: In Yongle 1 [the court] bestowed upon its king Zhao Lu Qun Ying the gold- and silver-gilt seal Duoluo Dilichituoni; the king at once sent envoys to express gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle the court granted King Zhao Lu Qun Ying a gilded gold-and-silver seal, and the king immediately dispatched envoys to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 六月，以上高皇帝尊謚， 遣官頒詔，有賜。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, because of the posthumous title of the Supreme Emperor Gaozu, [the court] dispatched officials to promulgate an edict, with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, honoring the Hongwu Emperor's posthumous title, officials were sent to proclaim an edict and present gifts.

sentences.zh: 八月覆命給事中王哲、行人成務賜其王錦綺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on return from their mission, supervising secretary Wang Zhe and courier Cheng Wu were sent to bestow brocades and silks upon the king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, after the mission returned, supervising secretary Wang Zhe and courier Cheng Wu were sent to bestow brocades upon the king.

sentences.zh: 九月命中官李興等 齎敕，勞賜其王，其文武諸臣並有賜。

translations.literal: In the ninth month eunuchs Li Xing and others were ordered to carry an edict, expressing comfort and bestowing gifts upon the king; civil and military officials likewise received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month eunuch Li Xing and others were sent with an edict of commendation and gifts for the king and his civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 二年有番船飄至福建海岸，詰之，乃暹羅與琉球通好者。

translations.literal: In year 2 a foreign ship drifted to the Fujian coast; upon questioning, it proved to be one traveling between Siam and Ryūkyū in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year a foreign vessel driven ashore on the Fujian coast proved, on inquiry, to be on friendly passage between Siam and Ryūkyū.

sentences.zh: 所司籍其貨以聞，帝 曰：「二國修好，乃甚美事，不幸遭風，正宜憐惜，豈可因以為利。

translations.literal: The responsible officials inventoried its cargo and reported; the emperor said: "Friendship between the two countries is a fine thing; to meet misfortune by wind is precisely when one should show compassion—how can one seek profit from it?
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials inventoried its cargo and reported the matter; the emperor said: "Friendship between the two kingdoms is a fine thing. When misfortune strikes at sea, compassion is what is called for—how can anyone seek profit from it?

sentences.zh: 所司其治舟給 粟，俟風便遣赴琉球。

translations.literal: Let the responsible officials repair the ship and supply grain, and when the wind is favorable send them on to Ryūkyū.
translations.idiomatic: Have the officials repair their ship, provision them with grain, and when a fair wind arises send them on to Ryūkyū.

sentences.zh: 」是月，其王以帝降璽書勞賜，遣使來謝，貢方物。

translations.literal: " That month, because the emperor had sent down an imperial letter of comfort and reward, its king sent envoys to give thanks and offer tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: " That same month, grateful for the emperor's comforting letter and gifts, the king sent envoys to give thanks and present tribute.

sentences.zh: 賜齎有 加，並賜《列女傳》百冊。

translations.literal: Gifts were increased, and one hundred copies of the Biographies of Exemplary Women were also granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court added further gifts and also bestowed one hundred copies of the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 使者請頒量衡為國永式，從之。

translations.literal: The envoys requested the promulgation of weights and measures as the kingdom's permanent standard; [the request] was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys asked for official weights and measures to be issued as a permanent standard for their kingdom, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 先是，占城貢使返，風飄其舟至彭亨，暹羅索取其使，羈留不遣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Champa's tribute envoys were returning, wind drove their ship to Pahang; Siam demanded their envoys and detained them without releasing them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Champa tribute envoys on their return were blown by storm to Pahang. Siam seized them and refused to release them.

sentences.zh: 蘇門答剌及 滿剌加又訴暹羅恃強發兵奪天朝所賜印誥。

translations.literal: Sumatra and Malacca also complained that Siam, relying on its strength, had sent troops to seize the seals and patents granted by the Heavenly Court.
translations.idiomatic: Sumatra and Malacca also lodged complaints that Siam had used its power to seize the seals and patents the court had granted them.

sentences.zh: 帝降敕責之曰：「占城、蘇門答剌、滿 剌加與爾俱受朝命，安得逞威拘其貢使，奪其誥印。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a reprimand, saying: "Champa, Sumatra, and Malacca, like you, have all received investiture from the court—how can you flaunt power, detain their tribute envoys, and seize their patents and seals?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a reprimand: "Champa, Sumatra, and Malacca, like you, all hold investiture from the court. How dare you throw your weight around, detain their tribute envoys, and seize their patents and seals?

sentences.zh: 天有顯道，福善禍淫，安南黎 賊可為鑑戒。

translations.literal: Heaven has its manifest Way: it blesses the good and punishes the wicked; the Lei bandits of Annam may serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way is plain—it rewards virtue and punishes wickedness. Let the Le bandits of Annam be your warning.

sentences.zh: 其即返占城使者，還蘇門答剌、滿剌加印誥。

translations.literal: Immediately return the Champa envoys and restore the seals and patents of Sumatra and Malacca.
translations.idiomatic: Return the Champa envoys at once and restore the seals and patents of Sumatra and Malacca.

sentences.zh: 自今奉法循理，保境睦 鄰，庶永享太平之福。

translations.literal: From now on observe the law and follow reason, guard your borders and live in amity with neighbors, and you may forever enjoy the blessings of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth uphold the law, keep your borders, and live in peace with your neighbors, and you may long enjoy the blessings of tranquility.

sentences.zh: 」時暹羅所遣貢使，失風飄至安南，盡為黎賊所殺，止余孛 黑一人。

translations.literal: " At that time Siam's tribute envoys, blown off course to Annam, were all killed by the Lei bandits; only one named Bo Hei remained.
translations.idiomatic: " Meanwhile Siam's tribute envoys, blown off course to Annam, were slaughtered by the Le bandits; only one survivor, Bo Hei, remained.

sentences.zh: 後官軍征安南，獲之以歸。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial army campaigned against Annam, he was captured and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the imperial army campaigned in Annam, he was brought back captive.

sentences.zh: 帝憫之，六年八月命中官張原送還國，賜王幣 帛，令厚恤被殺者之家。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on him; in the sixth year, eighth month, he ordered eunuch Zhang Yuan to escort him back to his country, bestowed silks upon the king, and commanded generous relief for the families of those killed.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, the emperor ordered eunuch Zhang Yuan in the eighth month of the sixth year to escort him home, sent silks to the king, and directed generous compensation for the slain envoys' families.

sentences.zh: 九月，中官鄭和使其國，其王遣使貢方物，謝前罪。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, eunuch Zheng He was sent to that country; its king dispatched envoys with tribute goods to apologize for the previous offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, when Zheng He was sent to the kingdom, the king dispatched envoys with tribute to apologize for the earlier wrong.

sentences.zh: 七年，使來祭仁孝皇后，命中官告之几筵。

translations.literal: In year 7 envoys came to perform sacrifices for Empress Renxiao; [the emperor] ordered a eunuch to announce this before the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year envoys came to offer sacrifice for Empress Renxiao, and the emperor sent a eunuch to announce the rites before her spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 時奸民何八觀等逃入暹羅，帝命使 者還告其主，毋納逋逃。

translations.literal: At that time wicked commoners such as He Baguan and others had fled into Siam; the emperor ordered the returning envoys to tell their ruler not to harbor fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: At the time outlaw He Baguan and others had fled to Siam; the emperor told the returning envoys to warn their king not to shelter fugitives.

sentences.zh: 其王即奉命遣使貢馬及方物，並送八觀等還，命張原齎敕 幣獎之。

translations.literal: Its king at once obeyed the command, sent envoys offering horses and tribute goods, and also returned Baguan and the others; [the emperor] ordered Zhang Yuan to carry an edict and silks to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The king promptly obeyed, sent horses and tribute, and returned Baguan and his companions; the emperor sent Zhang Yuan with an edict and silks to reward him.

sentences.zh: 十年命中官洪保等往賜幣。

translations.literal: In year 10 [the emperor] ordered eunuchs Hong Bao and others to go bestow silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year eunuch Hong Bao and others were sent to bestow silks.

sentences.zh: 十四年，王子三賴波羅摩剌答刂的賴遣使告父之喪。

translations.literal: In year 14, Prince Sanlai Boluomo La Da De Lai sent envoys to report his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Prince Sanlai Boluomo La Da De Lai sent envoys to announce his father's death.

sentences.zh: 命中官郭文往祭，別遣官 齎詔封其子為王，賜以素錦、素羅，隨遣使謝恩。

translations.literal: [The emperor] ordered eunuch Guo Wen to go perform sacrifices, separately dispatched officials carrying an edict to invest the son as king, bestowed plain brocade and plain gauze, and [the new king] soon sent envoys to express gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Guo Wen was sent to perform the funeral rites, and other officials carried an edict investing the son as king and granting plain brocade and gauze; the new king soon sent envoys to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 十七年命中官楊敏等護歸。

translations.literal: In year 17 [the emperor] ordered eunuchs Yang Min and others to escort them home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year eunuch Yang Min and others escorted the envoys home.

sentences.zh: 以暹 羅侵滿剌加，遣使責令輯睦，王復遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: Because Siam had invaded Malacca, envoys were sent to rebuke it and command reconciliation; the king again sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Because Siam had attacked Malacca, envoys were sent to rebuke the kingdom and demand peace; the king sent envoys again to apologize.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年，王悉裡麻哈賴遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In Xuande 8, King Xi Limahalai sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xuande, King Xi Limahalai sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 初，其國陪臣柰三鐸等貢舟次占城新州港，盡為其國人所掠。

translations.literal: Initially, attendant minister Nai Sanduo and others, when their tribute ship stopped at Champa's Xinzhou Harbor, were entirely plundered by people of that country.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the attendant minister Nai Sanduo and others anchored their tribute ship at Champa's Xinzhou Harbor, Champa raiders plundered them completely.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，柰三 鐸潛附小舟來京，訴占城劫掠狀。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong 1, Nai Sanduo secretly attached himself to a small boat and came to the capital, lodging a complaint about Champa's plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong, Nai Sanduo slipped aboard a small boat to the capital and reported Champa's raid.

sentences.zh: 帝命召占城使者與相質。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Champa envoys summoned to confront them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Champa envoys summoned to confront the accusers.

sentences.zh: 使者無以對，乃敕占城 王，令盡還所掠人物。

translations.literal: The envoys had no reply; [the emperor] then issued an edict to the King of Champa commanding the complete return of all people and goods plundered.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys had no answer, so the emperor ordered the king of Champa to return everything that had been seized.

sentences.zh: 已，占城移咨禮部言：「本國前歲遣使往須文達那，亦為暹 羅賊人掠去，必暹羅先還所掠，本國不敢不還。

translations.literal: Soon Champa sent a communication to the Ministry of Rites stating: "Our country the year before last sent envoys to Xuwendana; they too were plundered by Siam's brigands—Siam must first return what was plundered, and our country will not dare fail to return [what we took].
translations.idiomatic: Champa then wrote to the Ministry of Rites: "Our envoys bound for Xuwendana two years ago were also robbed by Siam. Once Siam returns what it seized, we will not fail to return what we took.

sentences.zh: 」三年，暹羅貢使又至，賜敕曉以 此意，令亟還占城人物。

translations.literal: " In year 3, Siam's tribute envoys came again; [the emperor] granted an edict explaining this intent and ordering the swift return of Champa's people and goods.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year, when Siam's tribute envoys arrived again, the emperor sent an edict explaining this and ordering the immediate return of Champa's people and goods.

sentences.zh: 十一年，王思利波羅麻那惹智剌遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In year 11, King Silibo Boluo Mana Rezhila sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year King Silibo Boluo Mana Rezhila sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年，命給事中劉洙、行人劉泰祭其故王波羅摩剌答刂的賴，封其嗣子把 羅蘭米孫剌為王。

translations.literal: In Jingtai 4, Supervising Secretary Liu Zhu and Courier Liu Tai were ordered to perform sacrifices for the late king Boluomo La Da De Lai and invest his heir Ba Luolan Mi Sunla as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingtai, supervising secretary Liu Zhu and courier Liu Tai were sent to mourn the late King Boluomo La Da De Lai and invest his heir Ba Luolan Mi Sunla as king.

sentences.zh: 天順元年賜其貢使钑花金帶。

translations.literal: In Tianshun 1 their tribute envoys were granted gold belts with inlaid floral design.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshun the tribute envoys were granted gold belts with floral inlay.

sentences.zh: 六年，王孛剌藍羅者直波智遣使朝 貢。

translations.literal: In year 6, King Bo La Lan Luo Zhe Zhibozhi sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year King Bo La Lan Luo Zhe Zhibozhi sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 成化九年，貢使言天順元年所頒勘合，為蟲所蝕，乞改給，從之。

translations.literal: In Chenghua 9, tribute envoys said the tally register issued in Tianshun 1 had been eaten by insects and requested replacement; [the request] was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Chenghua the envoys reported that their Tianshun tally register had been destroyed by insects and asked for a replacement; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 十七年，貢 使還，至中途竊買子女，且多載私鹽，命遣官戒諭諸番。

translations.literal: In year 17, the tribute envoys on their return midway secretly bought children and also carried much private salt; [the emperor] ordered officials dispatched to admonish the various foreign countries.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, returning envoys were found en route to have bought children illicitly and to be carrying large amounts of contraband salt; officials were sent to warn all the maritime kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 先是，汀州人謝文彬，以 販鹽下海，飄入其國，仕至坤岳，猶天朝學士也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xie Wenbin of Tingzhou, having gone to sea in the salt trade, drifted into that country and served up to the rank of Kun Yue, which is like an academician of the Heavenly Court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xie Wenbin of Tingzhou had gone to sea as a salt smuggler, washed ashore in Siam, and risen to the post of Kun Yue—the equivalent of a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 後充使來朝，貿易禁物，事覺下 吏。

translations.literal: Later, serving as envoy on a tribute mission to court, he traded in prohibited goods; when the affair was discovered he was handed over to the legal authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he came to court as an envoy, he traded in banned goods; once the matter came to light he was handed over to the courts.

sentences.zh: 十八年遣使朝貢，且告父喪，命給事中林霄、行人姚隆往封其子國隆勃剌略坤 息剌尤地為王。

translations.literal: In year 18 [the king] sent envoys to court with tribute and to report his father's death; Supervising Secretary Lin Xiao and Courier Yao Long were ordered to go invest his son Guo Long Bo Lue Kun Xi La Youdi as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year envoys came with tribute and news of the king's death; supervising secretary Lin Xiao and courier Yao Long were sent to invest his son Guo Long Bo Lue Kun Xi La Youdi as king.

sentences.zh: 弘治十年入貢。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi 10 [they] came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Hongzhi they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 時四夷館無暹羅譯字官，閣臣徐溥等請移牒廣東， 訪取能通彼國言語文字者，赴京備用，從之。

translations.literal: At that time the Four Barbarians Hostel had no Siam interpreter-clerk; Grand Secretary Xu Pu and others requested that a notice be sent to Guangdong to search out persons who could understand that country's language and script and send them to the capital for service; [the request] was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Barbarians Hostel had no Siamese interpreter on staff, so Grand Secretary Xu Pu and others asked Guangdong to find someone fluent in the kingdom's language and script and send him to the capital; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，暹羅船有飄至廣東者，市 舶中官熊宣與守臣議，稅其物供軍需。

translations.literal: In Zhengde 4, a Siam ship drifted to Guangdong; the maritime trade eunuch Xiong Xuan and the defending officials discussed levying tax on its goods to supply military needs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengde a Siamese vessel was driven ashore in Guangdong; maritime trade eunuch Xiong Xuan and the local officials proposed taxing its cargo for military supplies.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔斥宣妄攬事柄，撤還南京。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict rebuked Xuan for arrogating authority without cause and recalled him to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the throne, an edict rebuked Xuan for overstepping his authority and recalled him to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十年進 金葉表朝貢，館中無識其字者。

translations.literal: In year 10 [they] came to court with tribute presenting a gold-leaf memorial; in the hostel none could read the script.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year they presented a gold-leaf memorial at court, but no one in the hostel could read the script.

sentences.zh: 閣臣梁儲等請選留其使一二人入館肄習，報可。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liang Chu and others requested that one or two of their envoys be selected and retained to study in the hostel; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liang Chu and others asked that one or two envoys be kept at the hostel for language training; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉 靖元年，暹羅、占城貨船至廣東。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 1, Siam and Champa merchant ships arrived at Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing, merchant ships from Siam and Champa reached Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 市舶中官牛榮縱家人私市，論死如律。

translations.literal: The maritime trade superintendent eunuch Niu Rong allowed his household members to engage in private trade; he was sentenced to death according to the law.
translations.idiomatic: The maritime trade eunuch Niu Rong had let his family conduct private trade on the side, and was sentenced to death as the statutes required.

sentences.zh: 三十二年 遣使貢白象及方物，象死於途，使者以珠寶飾其牙，盛以金盤，並尾來獻。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year envoys were sent to present tribute of a white elephant and local products; the elephant died on the road, and the envoys adorned its tusks with jewels, placed them in a gold dish, and together with the tail came to present them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Jiajing, Siam sent envoys bearing a white elephant and other tribute goods. The elephant died en route, so the envoys set its tusks with jewels, laid them in a golden dish, and brought tusks and tail together as their offering.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其 意，厚遣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised their intention and sent them away with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired their devotion and rewarded them with lavish gifts on their departure.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，其鄰國東蠻牛求婚不得，慚怒，大發兵攻破其國。

translations.literal: During the Longqing reign, its neighboring state Dong Man Niu, having failed in a marriage request, felt ashamed and enraged, and mobilized a large army that broke into and overran the country.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign, the neighboring state of Dong Man Niu, rebuffed in a marriage suit, burned with shame and rage and marched a great army that smashed Siam's defenses and overran the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 王自經，擄其世子 及天朝所賜印以歸。

translations.literal: The king hanged himself; they carried off the heir apparent and the seal bestowed by the Celestial Dynasty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The king took his own life. The invaders seized the crown prince and the seal the Ming court had granted, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次子嗣位，奉表請印，予之。

translations.literal: The second son succeeded to the throne, submitted a memorial requesting a seal, and was granted one.
translations.idiomatic: The second son ascended the throne, petitioned for a new seal, and received one.

sentences.zh: 自是為東蠻牛所制，嗣王勵志復 仇。

translations.literal: From this point the country came under Dong Man Niu's control; the succeeding king resolved to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Siam lay under Dong Man Niu's sway, while the new king burned to avenge the humiliation.

sentences.zh: 萬曆間，敵兵復至，王整兵奮擊，大破之，殺其子，餘眾宵遁，暹羅由是雄海 上。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign, enemy troops came again; the king assembled his forces and struck fiercely, routing them utterly, killing the enemy's son; the remnant fled by night, and Siam thereafter dominated the seas.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli era the enemy returned. The king mustered his troops, fought with fury, and broke them completely, slaying the invader's son. The survivors fled under cover of night, and from that time Siam reigned supreme on the sea.

sentences.zh: 移兵攻破真臘，降其王。

translations.literal: He shifted his army and broke into Khmer, subduing its king.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned his army against Khmer, crushed the kingdom, and forced its king to submit.

sentences.zh: 從此歲歲用兵，遂霸諸國。

translations.literal: From then on he waged war year after year and thus came to dominate the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he campaigned every year until he had made himself overlord of the surrounding states.

sentences.zh: 六年遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year envoys were sent to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wanli, envoys arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日本破朝鮮，暹羅請潛師直搗日本，牽其後。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Japan broke Korea; Siam requested to send troops secretly to strike directly at Japan and threaten its rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Wanli, when Japan invaded Korea, Siam offered to dispatch a hidden force to strike Japan from behind and pin the enemy's rear.

sentences.zh: 中樞石 星議從之，兩廣督臣蕭彥持不可，乃已。

translations.literal: The chief counselor Shi Xing argued for accepting the proposal, but the governor-general of the Two Guangs, Xiao Yan, maintained it should not be done, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shi Xing favored the plan, but the governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi, Xiao Yan, argued against it, and the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 其後，奉貢不替。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute missions continued without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: After that, tribute missions continued without a break.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年猶入貢。

translations.literal: Even in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen tribute was still sent.
translations.idiomatic: As late as the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, envoys still came bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國，周千里，風俗勁悍，習於水戰。

translations.literal: The country measures a thousand li in circumference; its customs are fierce and hardy, and its people are practiced in naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom spans a thousand li in circuit. Its people are fierce by nature and skilled in fighting on the water.

sentences.zh: 大將用聖鐵裹身，刀矢不能入。

translations.literal: Great generals wrap their bodies in sacred iron, and blades and arrows cannot penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: Senior commanders clad themselves in what they called sacred iron, and neither blade nor arrow could pierce it.

sentences.zh: 聖鐵者， 人腦骨也。

translations.literal: Sacred iron is human skull bone.
translations.idiomatic: That sacred iron, in fact, was human skull bone.

sentences.zh: 王，瑣裡人。

translations.literal: The king is a man of Suoli.
translations.idiomatic: The king was a native of Suoli in the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 官分十等。

translations.literal: Official ranks are divided into ten grades.
translations.idiomatic: Government offices were ranked in ten grades.

sentences.zh: 自王至庶民，有事皆決於其婦。

translations.literal: From the king down to commoners, whenever anything arises it is decided by their wives.
translations.idiomatic: From the king to the humblest subject, every important matter was settled by the wife.

sentences.zh: 其婦人志量， 實出男子上。

translations.literal: Those women's resolve and capacity truly surpass those of men.
translations.idiomatic: In judgment and force of will, the women truly outstripped the men.

sentences.zh: 婦私華人，則夫置酒同飲，恬不為怪，曰：「我婦美，而為華人所悅 也。

translations.literal: If a wife takes a Chinese lover, the husband sets out wine and drinks together with them, finding nothing strange in it, saying: "My wife is beautiful, and Chinese men are fond of her.
translations.idiomatic: If a wife took a Chinese lover, the husband would set out wine and drink with them as though it were the most natural thing in the world, saying, "My wife is beautiful, and Chinese men admire her.

sentences.zh: 」崇信釋教，男女多為僧尼，亦居菴寺，持齋受戒。

translations.literal: " They devoutly believe in Buddhism; many men and women become monks and nuns, living in temples and keeping vegetarian fasts while receiving precepts.
translations.idiomatic: " The people were devout Buddhists. Many men and women became monks and nuns, dwelling in temples, keeping vegetarian fasts, and taking vows.

sentences.zh: 衣服頗類中國。

translations.literal: Their clothing rather resembles that of China.
translations.idiomatic: Their dress closely resembled Chinese styles.

sentences.zh: 富貴者， 尤敬佛，百金之產，即以其半施之。

translations.literal: The wealthy especially revere the Buddha; if their estate is worth a hundred ounces of gold, they at once give half of it away.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families were especially pious: a fortune of a hundred gold pieces would see half of it given to the temples at once.

sentences.zh: 氣候不正，或寒或熱，地卑濕，人皆樓居。

translations.literal: The climate is irregular, now cold, now hot; the land is low and damp, and everyone lives in raised houses.
translations.idiomatic: The climate swung erratically between cold and heat. The land was low and wet, and everyone lived in stilted houses.

sentences.zh: 男 女椎結，以白布裹首。

translations.literal: Men and women wear topknots and wrap white cloth around their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wore their hair in topknots and bound their heads in white cloth.

sentences.zh: 富貴者死，用水銀灌其口而葬之。

translations.literal: When the wealthy die, mercury is poured into their mouths and they are buried.
translations.idiomatic: When a rich person died, mercury was poured into the mouth before burial.

sentences.zh: 貧者則移置海濱，即有群 鴉飛啄，俄頃而盡，家人拾其骨號泣而棄之於海，謂之鳥葬。

translations.literal: The poor are instead moved to the seashore, where flocks of crows swoop down to peck; in no time the flesh is gone; family members gather the bones, wailing, and cast them into the sea—the custom is called bird burial.
translations.idiomatic: The poor were taken to the shore, where clouds of crows descended to feed. In moments the body was stripped clean. Kin gathered the bones, weeping, and cast them into the sea—a rite they called bird burial.

sentences.zh: 亦延僧設齋禮佛。

translations.literal: They also invite monks to hold feasts and worship the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Monks were also invited to hold feasts and perform Buddhist rites.

sentences.zh: 交 易用海。

translations.literal: Trade uses cowrie shells.
translations.idiomatic: Cowrie shells served as currency in trade.

sentences.zh: 是年不用，則國必大疫。

translations.literal: If cowrie shells are not used that year, the country is sure to suffer a great epidemic.
translations.idiomatic: If the shells went unused in a given year, the kingdom was believed certain to suffer a terrible plague.

sentences.zh: 其貢物，有像、象牙、犀角、孔雀尾、翠羽、龜 筒、六足龜、寶石、珊瑚、片腦、米腦、糠腦、腦油、腦柴、薔薇水、碗石、丁皮、 阿魏、紫梗、藤竭、藤黃、硫黃、沒藥、烏爹泥、安息香、羅斛香、速香、檀香、 黃熟香、降真香、乳香、樹香、木香、丁香、烏香、胡椒、蘇木、肉荳蔻、白荳蔻、 蓽茇、烏木、大楓子及撒哈剌、西洋諸布。

translations.literal: Its tribute goods include ivory figures, elephant tusks, rhinoceros horn, peacock tails, kingfisher feathers, tortoise shells, six-clawed tortoises, precious stones, coral, camphor flakes, nutmeg, nutmeg husks, camphor oil, camphor wood, rosewater, bowl-stones, cassia bark, asafetida, purple stems, rattan gum, gamboge, sulfur, myrrh, bismuth ointment, benzoin, lohak incense, gharuwood, sandalwood, aged sandalwood, eaglewood, frankincense, tree resin, costus root, cloves, aloeswood, pepper, sappanwood, nutmeg, white cardamom, long pepper, ebony, large maple seeds, and Sahala cloth and other fabrics of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included carved ivory, elephant tusks, rhinoceros horn, peacock plumes, kingfisher feathers, tortoise shells, six-clawed tortoises, gems, coral, camphor in every form—flakes, nutmeg, husks, oil, and wood—rosewater, bowl-stones, cassia bark, asafetida, purple stems, rattan extracts, gamboge, sulfur, myrrh, bismuth paste, benzoin, lohak and gharu incenses, sandalwood in several grades, eaglewood, frankincense, tree resins, costus, cloves, aloeswood, pepper, sappanwood, nutmeg and cardamom, long pepper, ebony, large maple seeds, Sahala cloth, and other fabrics from the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 其國有三寶廟，祀中官鄭和。

translations.literal: In the country there is a Sanbao Temple, where the eunuch Zheng He is worshipped.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom maintained a Sanbao Temple dedicated to the eunuch Zheng He.

sentences.zh: 爪哇在占城西南。

translations.literal: Java lies southwest of Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Java lay southwest of Champa.

sentences.zh: 元世祖時，遣使臣孟琪往，黥其面。

translations.literal: During the reign of Kublai Khan, the envoy Meng Qi was sent thither and had his face tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kublai Khan, an envoy named Meng Qi was sent there and had his face branded.

sentences.zh: 世祖大舉兵伐之，破其 國而還。

translations.literal: The Emperor launched a major campaign against it, broke its kingdom, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan emperor then mounted a great expedition, shattered the kingdom, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，太祖遣使以即位詔諭其國。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 2, the founding Emperor sent envoys bearing an enthronement edict to notify the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongwu, the founding emperor sent envoys with an enthronement edict to announce his accession to Java.

sentences.zh: 其使臣先奉貢於元，還至福建而元亡， 因入居京師。

translations.literal: Its envoys had first come to offer tribute to the Yuan; on returning as far as Fujian the Yuan fell, so they took up residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Java's envoys had already been en route to pay tribute to the Yuan when, reaching Fujian, they learned the dynasty had fallen. They remained in the capital instead.

sentences.zh: 太祖復遣使送之還，且賜以《大統歷》。

translations.literal: The founding Emperor again sent envoys to escort them home and granted them the Datong Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor sent them home under escort and bestowed the Datong Calendar upon them.

sentences.zh: 三年以平定沙漠頒詔曰： 「自古為天下主者，視天地所覆載，日月所照臨，若遠若近，生人之類，莫不欲其 安土而樂生。

translations.literal: In the third year, upon pacifying the desert an edict was issued saying: "Since ancient times, whoever is master of all under Heaven looks upon all that heaven and earth enfold and that sun and moon illuminate, whether far or near, and among the multitude of living human kind, there is none who does not wish to settle peacefully in their land and rejoice in life.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after the desert campaigns were settled, an edict proclaimed: "From antiquity, the ruler of all under Heaven has regarded every place heaven and earth cover and every people the sun and moon shine upon, near or far, and none among living humanity who does not wish to dwell in peace and live in contentment.

sentences.zh: 然必中國安，而後四方萬國順附。

translations.literal: Yet China must first be secure, and only then will the myriad states of the four quarters willingly attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: But the Middle Kingdom must first be secure; only then will the myriad states of the four quarters willingly submit.

sentences.zh: 邇元君妥懽帖木兒，荒淫昏弱，志 不在民。

translations.literal: Recently the Yuan ruler Tuohuan Timur was dissolute and weak, with no thought for the people.
translations.idiomatic: The late Yuan ruler, Tuohuan Timur, was debauched and feeble, with no care for his people.

sentences.zh: 天下英雄，分裂疆宇。

translations.literal: Heroes throughout the realm divided the territory among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes rose everywhere and carved the realm into rival domains.

sentences.zh: 朕憫生民之塗炭，興舉義兵，攘除亂略。

translations.literal: I commiserated with the people's misery in the war zone, raised righteous troops, and swept away chaos and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: I grieved for the people drowning in war, raised righteous armies, and cleared away chaos and violence.

sentences.zh: 天下軍民 共尊朕居帝位，國號大明，建元洪武。

translations.literal: The armies and people of all under Heaven together honored me with the imperial throne; the state was called Great Ming and the reign title Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The armies and people of the realm together raised me to the throne. The dynasty is called Great Ming, and the reign title Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 前年克取元都，四方底定。

translations.literal: The year before last we took the Yuan capital, and the four directions were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Two years ago we captured the Yuan capital, and the four quarters were pacified.

sentences.zh: 占城、安南、高 麗諸國，俱來朝貢。

translations.literal: Champa, Annam, Korea, and other states all came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Champa, Annam, Korea, and other states have all come to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 今年遣將北征，始知元君已沒，獲其孫買的裡八刺，封為崇禮 侯。

translations.literal: This year we dispatched generals on a northern campaign, only to learn that the Yuan ruler had already died; we captured his grandson Maidili Basi and enfeoffed him as the Marquis of Chongli.
translations.idiomatic: This year I sent generals north and learned that the Yuan emperor was already dead. We captured his grandson Maidili Basi and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chongli.

sentences.zh: 朕仿前代帝王，治理天下，惟欲中外人民，各安其所。

translations.literal: Following the example of emperors of former ages, I govern all under Heaven, desiring only that the people within and beyond the borders each abide in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Following the example of emperors of old, I govern the realm, wishing only that people within and beyond the borders may each live in their proper place.

sentences.zh: 又慮諸蕃僻在遠方，未 悉朕意，故遣使者往諭，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: Yet I also feared that the various tributary lands, remote and far away, might not fully understand my intent, and therefore sent envoys to instruct them, that all might know.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I feared the distant tributary states might not yet understand my intent, and so I have sent envoys to make it known to all.

sentences.zh: 」九月，其王昔裡八達剌蒲遣使奉金葉表來朝， 貢方物，宴賚如禮。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month, King Xili Badalipu sent envoys presenting a memorial on gold leaf, offered local products, and was feasted and rewarded according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month, King Xili Badalipu sent envoys with a memorial written on gold leaf, presented local products, and was entertained and rewarded according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 五年又遣使隨朝使常克敬來貢，上元所授宣敕三道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year envoys were again sent, following the Ming envoy Chang Kejing to present tribute, returning three investiture patents from the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year envoys came again with the Ming envoy Chang Kejing, bearing tribute and surrendering three Yuan investiture patents.

sentences.zh: 八年又貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year tribute was again sent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十年，王八達 那巴那務遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, King Badanabanawu dispatched envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year King Badanabanawu sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國又有東、西二王，東蕃王勿院勞網結，西蕃王勿勞波務， 各遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the country there were also two kings, East and West: the Eastern king Wuyuan Laowangjie and the Western king Wulao Bowu each sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The realm also had eastern and western kings: the eastern king Wuyuan Laowangjie and the western king Wulao Bowu each dispatched envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天子以其禮意不誠，詔留其使，已而釋還之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, considering their courtesy insincere, ordered the envoys detained, but soon released them to return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged their courtesy insincere, ordered the envoys detained, then soon released them to return home.

sentences.zh: 十二年，王八達那巴那 務遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year King Badanabanawu sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year King Badanabanawu again sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年又貢。

translations.literal: The next year tribute was again sent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 時遣使賜三佛齊王印綬，爪哇誘而殺之。

translations.literal: At that time envoys were dispatched to confer a seal and sash upon the king of Srivijaya; Java lured and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ming envoys were sent to invest the king of Srivijaya with a seal and sash; Java lured them in and killed them.

sentences.zh: 天子怒，留其使 月餘，將加罪，已，遣還，賜敕責之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was enraged, detained their envoys for more than a month intending to punish them, but eventually sent them back with an imperial letter of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, held Java's envoys for more than a month intending punishment, then sent them home with an imperial letter of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 十四年遣使貢黑奴三百人及他方物。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year envoys sent tribute of three hundred black slaves and other local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year envoys brought three hundred black slaves and other tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 明年又 貢黑奴男女百人、大珠八顆、胡椒七萬五千斤。

translations.literal: The next year they again sent tribute of one hundred black slave men and women, eight large pearls, and seventy-five thousand jin of pepper.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they sent another tribute mission with one hundred black slaves, male and female, eight large pearls, and seventy-five thousand jin of pepper.

sentences.zh: 二十六年再貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year tribute was sent again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 明年又貢。

translations.literal: The next year tribute was sent again.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, tribute came once more.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，詔諭其國。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor took the throne, an edict was issued to notify the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor ascended the throne, an edict was sent to notify Java.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年又遣副使聞良輔、行人甯善，賜其王絨、綿、 織金文綺、紗羅。

translations.literal: In Yongle 1 the vice envoy Wen Liangfu and the imperial commissioner Ning Shan were again sent to bestow on its king velvet, cotton, brocaded silk, and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle, Vice Envoy Wen Liangfu and Commissioner Ning Shan were dispatched again to grant the king velvet, cotton, brocaded silks, and gauzes.

sentences.zh: 使者既行，其西王都馬板遣使入賀，覆命中官馬彬等賜以鍍金銀 印。

translations.literal: After the envoys had departed, the Western king Duma Ban sent envoys to offer congratulations; the Emperor thereupon ordered the eunuch Ma Bin and others to bestow a gilt silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: After the envoys had left, the western king Duma Ban sent congratulations; the emperor then ordered the eunuch Ma Bin and others to confer a gilt silver seal.

sentences.zh: 西王遣使謝賜印，貢方物。

translations.literal: The Western king sent envoys to thank the Emperor for the seal and present local products.
