translations.idiomatic: The western king sent envoys to thank the court for the seal and present local products.

sentences.zh: 而東王孛令達哈亦遣使朝貢，請印，命遣官賜之。

translations.literal: The Eastern king Bo Ling Daha also sent envoys with tribute and requested a seal; the court ordered officials dispatched to confer one.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern king Bo Ling Daha also sent tribute and requested a seal; the court ordered officials to deliver one.

sentences.zh: 自後，二王並貢。

translations.literal: Thereafter both kings sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From then on both kings sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年遣中官鄭和使其國。

translations.literal: In the third year the eunuch Zheng He was sent as envoy to the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the eunuch Zheng He was dispatched as envoy to Java.

sentences.zh: 明年，西王與東王構兵，東王戰敗，國被滅。

translations.literal: The next year the Western king and Eastern king made war on each other; the Eastern king was defeated and his state destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the western and eastern kings went to war. The eastern king was defeated and his state wiped out.

sentences.zh: 適朝使 經東王地，部卒入市，西王國人殺之，凡百七十人。

translations.literal: It happened that Ming envoys were passing through Eastern king's territory; troops of the Western king entered the market and the Western king's countrymen killed them—a total of one hundred seventy persons.
translations.idiomatic: By chance a Ming mission was passing through the eastern king's lands when western troops entered the market and western subjects killed them—one hundred seventy men in all.

sentences.zh: 西王懼，遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: The Western king was afraid and sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The western king, terrified, sent envoys to apologize.

sentences.zh: 帝賜敕切 責之，命輸黃金六萬兩以贖。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted an imperial letter sharply rebuking him and ordered payment of sixty thousand liang of gold as redemption.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a stern imperial letter of rebuke and ordered sixty thousand liang of gold paid as ransom.

sentences.zh: 六年再遣鄭和使其國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zheng He was again sent as envoy to the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zheng He was again sent as envoy to Java.

sentences.zh: 西王獻黃金萬兩，禮官以輸數 不足，請下其使於獄。

translations.literal: The Western king presented ten thousand liang of gold; the ceremonial officials, finding the sum insufficient, requested that the envoys be imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The western king offered ten thousand liang of gold. The ceremonial officials, finding the payment short, asked that the envoys be jailed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕於遠人，欲其畏罪而已，寧利其金耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Toward distant peoples I wish only that they fear punishment for their crimes—would I profit from their gold?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "With distant peoples I want only that they fear punishment for their crimes. Would I covet their gold?

sentences.zh: 」悉捐之。

translations.literal: " He entirely remitted it.
translations.idiomatic: " He remitted the payment entirely.

sentences.zh: 自後，比年一貢，或間歲一貢，或一歲數貢。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute came in most years, or every other year, or several times within a single year.
translations.idiomatic: After that, tribute arrived nearly every year, or every other year, or several times in a single year.

sentences.zh: 中官吳賓、鄭和先後使其國。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Wu Bin and Zheng He successively served as envoys to the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Wu Bin and Zheng He were sent as envoys to Java in succession.

sentences.zh: 時舊港 地有為爪哇侵據者，滿剌加國王矯朝命索之。

translations.literal: At that time in Old Port there were places occupied by Java's invasion; the king of Malacca falsely claimed an imperial command to demand them back.
translations.idiomatic: At that time parts of Old Port lay under Java's occupation, and the king of Malacca forged an imperial order to demand their return.

sentences.zh: 帝乃賜敕曰：「前中官尹慶還，言王 恭待敕使，有加無替。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon granted an edict saying: "When the eunuch Yin Qing returned earlier, he reported that you received the imperial envoy with utmost courtesy, beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict: "When the eunuch Yin Qing returned earlier, he reported that you received the imperial envoy with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 比聞滿剌加國索舊港之地，王甚疑懼。

translations.literal: But I have lately heard that Malacca is demanding the Old Port territories, and you are greatly suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that Malacca is pressing a claim to Old Port, and that you are deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 朕推誠待人，若果許 之，必有敕諭，王何疑焉。

translations.literal: I treat people with sincerity; if I truly intended to grant it, there would surely be an imperial edict—why should you doubt?
translations.idiomatic: I deal with others in good faith. If I truly meant to grant the land, an imperial edict would have been issued—why should you doubt?

sentences.zh: 小人浮詞，慎勿輕聽。

translations.literal: Do not lightly listen to the loose words of petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Do not heed the idle talk of petty men.

sentences.zh: 」十三年，其王改名揚惟西沙， 遣使謝恩，貢方物。

translations.literal: " In the thirteenth year the king changed his name to Yang Weixisha, sent envoys to express gratitude, and presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: " In the thirteenth year the king changed his name to Yang Weixisha, sent envoys to express gratitude, and presented local products.

sentences.zh: 時朝使所攜卒有遭風飄至班卒兒國者，爪哇人珍班聞之，用金 贖還，歸之王所。

translations.literal: At that time soldiers carried by Ming envoys who were blown by wind to Bancuer were heard of by Zhen Ban of Java, who used gold to ransom them and return them to the king's court.
translations.idiomatic: Some soldiers traveling with a Ming mission were blown by storm to Bancuer. Zhen Ban of Java heard of it, paid gold to ransom them, and returned them to the king's court.

sentences.zh: 十六年，王遣使朝貢，因送還諸卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the king sent envoys with tribute and thereby returned the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the king sent envoys with tribute and returned the soldiers with them.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賜敕獎王，並優賜 珍班。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended this, granted an edict praising the king, and also bestowed special rewards on Zhen Ban.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the deed, issued an edict commending the king, and granted special rewards to Zhen Ban.

sentences.zh: 自是，朝貢使臣大率每歲一至。

translations.literal: From this point tribute envoys generally came once each year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on tribute envoys generally came about once a year.

sentences.zh: 八年，廣東參政張琰言：「爪哇朝貢頻數，供億費煩，敝中國以事遠人，非計。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Guangdong Assistant Administrator Zhang Yan memorialized: "Java's tribute missions come with excessive frequency; the costs of reception and supplies are burdensome—exhausting China to serve distant peoples is no sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Guangdong Assistant Administrator Zhang Yan memorialized: "Java's tribute missions come too often; the cost of receiving them is a burden. To wear out China in serving distant peoples is poor policy.

sentences.zh: 」 帝納之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 其使還，賜敕曰：「海外諸邦，並三年一貢。

translations.literal: When their envoys returned, he granted an edict saying: "All overseas states shall send tribute once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: When Java's envoys returned home, he issued an edict: "All overseas states shall send tribute once every three years.

sentences.zh: 王亦宜體恤軍民，一遵此制。

translations.literal: The king, too, should sympathize with his armies and people and strictly observe this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The king, too, should care for his armies and people and observe this rule strictly.

sentences.zh: 」 十一年復三貢，後乃漸稀。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh year they again sent tribute three times; afterward missions gradually grew rare.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh year they sent tribute three times again; after that missions grew increasingly rare.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，王巴剌武遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai, King Balawu sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingtai, King Balawu sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天順四年，王都馬班遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun, King Duma Ban sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianshun, King Duma Ban sent envoys to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 使者還至安慶， 酗酒，與入貢番僧斗，僧死者六人。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned as far as Anqing, they drank heavily and fought with the tribute Buddhist monks; six monks died.
translations.idiomatic: On their return journey the envoys reached Anqing, got drunk, and brawled with the Buddhist monks who had come with the tribute mission; six of the monks were killed.

sentences.zh: 禮官請治伴送行人罪，使者敕國王自治，從之。

translations.literal: The rites officials requested punishing the escort personnel for their offense; the envoys were ordered by edict to have the king punish them himself; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites asked that the escorts be punished, but the court instead ordered the envoys to have their king deal with the matter himself, and this was approved.

sentences.zh: 成化元年入貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua they offered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 the kingdom sent a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年，貢使遭風舟壞，止通事一舟達廣東。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi, the tribute envoys encountered wind and their ships were wrecked; only one vessel with an interpreter reached Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 12 the tribute envoys were caught in a storm and their ships were destroyed; only a single boat carrying an interpreter made it to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 禮官請敕所司， 量予賜賚遣還，其貢物仍進京師，制可。

translations.literal: The rites officials requested that the relevant offices be ordered to grant measured gifts and send them back, while the tribute goods should still be sent to the capital; the order was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites asked that the appropriate offices be instructed to give the envoys suitable gifts and send them home, while still forwarding the tribute goods to the capital; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 自是貢使鮮有至者。

translations.literal: From then on tribute envoys rarely came.
translations.idiomatic: After that, tribute envoys seldom arrived.

sentences.zh: 其國近占城，二十晝夜可至。

translations.literal: The country is close to Champa; one can reach it in twenty days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom lay near Champa, about twenty days' sailing away.

sentences.zh: 元師西征，以至元二十九年十二月發泉州，明年 正月即抵其國，相去止月餘。

translations.literal: When the Yuan armies went west on campaign, they set out from Quanzhou in the twelfth month of the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan and reached the country in the first month of the following year—a journey of little more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuan western expedition, the army left Quanzhou in the twelfth month of Zhiyuan 29 and reached Java the following first month, barely a month later.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年入貢，表書「一千三百七十六年」，蓋漢宣 帝元康元年，乃其建國之始也。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuande they offered tribute; the memorial gave the year as "1376," which corresponds to the first year of Yuankang under Han Emperor Xuandi—the beginning of their state foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 7 they sent tribute; their memorial dated the realm to "1376 years," counting from Yuankang 1 of Han Emperor Xuandi, which they took as the founding of their state.

sentences.zh: 地廣人稠。

translations.literal: The territory is vast and the population dense.
translations.idiomatic: The land was broad and densely populated.

sentences.zh: 性凶悍，男子無少長貴賤皆佩刀，稍忤 輒相賊，故其甲兵為諸蕃之最。

translations.literal: Their nature is fierce and savage; men of every age and rank, noble or common, wear swords, and at the slightest offense they kill one another; hence their armor and troops are the foremost among all the foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fierce by nature. Every man, young or old, highborn or low, wore a sword, and the slightest provocation could end in bloodshed, so their arms and fighting men ranked first among all the foreign kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 字類瑣裡，無紙筆，刻於茭曌葉。

translations.literal: Their script resembles that of Palembang; they have no paper or brushes and inscribe on palm leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Their writing resembled that of Palembang. They had no paper or ink brushes and carved their characters onto palm leaves.

sentences.zh: 氣候常似夏，稻 歲二稔。

translations.literal: The climate is always like summer; rice yields two harvests a year.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was perennially summer-like, and rice could be harvested twice a year.

sentences.zh: 無幾榻匕箸。

translations.literal: They have no tables, couches, spoons, or chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: They used no tables, couches, spoons, or chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 人有三種：華人流寓者，服食鮮華；

translations.literal: There are three kinds of people: Chinese who have settled there dress and eat splendidly;
translations.idiomatic: There were three kinds of people. Chinese who had settled there dressed and ate in fine style;

sentences.zh: 他國賈人居久者，亦尚 雅潔；

translations.literal: merchants of other countries who have lived there long likewise value elegance and cleanliness;
translations.idiomatic: merchants from other countries who had lived there for years also prized refinement and cleanliness;

sentences.zh: 其本國人最污穢，好啖蛇蟻蟲蚓，與犬同寢食，狀黝黑，猱頭赤腳。

translations.literal: the native people of the country are the most filthy—they like to eat snakes, ants, worms, and earthworms, sleep and eat with dogs, are dark black in appearance, with monkey-like hair and bare feet.
translations.idiomatic: but the native inhabitants were the most squalid. They ate snakes, ants, insects, and earthworms, slept and ate alongside dogs, and were dark-skinned, with shaggy hair and bare feet.

sentences.zh: 崇信鬼 道。

translations.literal: They believe in ghost cults.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped spirits and demons.

sentences.zh: 殺人者避之三日即免罪。

translations.literal: A murderer who hides for three days is then absolved of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: A killer who went into hiding for three days was then cleared of guilt.

sentences.zh: 父母死，舁至野，縱犬食之；

translations.literal: When parents die, they are carried to the wilds and set loose for dogs to eat;
translations.idiomatic: When parents died, the body was carried into the wild and left for dogs to devour;

sentences.zh: 不盡，則大戚，燔其餘。

translations.literal: if not fully consumed, they weep bitterly and burn what remains.
translations.idiomatic: if the dogs did not finish it, the family wailed in grief and burned what was left.

sentences.zh: 妻妾多燔以殉。

translations.literal: Many wives and concubines are burned to follow them in death.
translations.idiomatic: Many wives and concubines were cremated to accompany the dead.

sentences.zh: 其國一名莆家龍，又曰下港，曰順塔。

translations.literal: The country is also called Pujialong, also called Xiagang, also called Shunta.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom was also known as Pujialong, as Xiagang, and as Shunta.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，紅毛番築土庫於大澗東，佛郎 機築於大澗西，歲歲互市。

translations.literal: In the Wanli era, the Dutch built storehouses east of the Great Creek and the Portuguese built on the west; they traded with one another every year.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, the Dutch built warehouses east of the Great Creek and the Portuguese built on the west, and the two sides traded with each other every year.

sentences.zh: 中國商旅亦往來不絕。

translations.literal: Chinese merchants and travelers also went back and forth without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchants and travelers also passed through constantly.

sentences.zh: 其國有新村，最號饒富。

translations.literal: The country has a place called New Village, famed as the richest of all.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had a settlement called New Village, renowned as the wealthiest in the land.

sentences.zh: 中華及 諸番商舶，輻輳其地，寶貨填溢。

translations.literal: Chinese and foreign merchant ships converged on the place, and precious goods overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese and foreign merchant vessels crowded its harbor, and treasures piled up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 其村主即廣東人，永樂九年自遣使表貢方物。

translations.literal: The headman of the village was a Guangdong man who in the ninth year of Yongle sent envoys of his own accord with a memorial and tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: The village headman was a man from Guangdong who, in Yongle 9, sent envoys on his own initiative with a memorial and local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 阇婆，古曰阇婆達。

translations.literal: Zhepo—in antiquity called Zheboda.
translations.idiomatic: Zhepo was known in antiquity as Zheboda.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉時，始朝中國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of the Liu Song, they first paid court to China.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia reign of the Liu Song, it first sent missions to the Chinese court.

sentences.zh: 唐曰訶陵，又曰社婆，其王居阇婆 城，宋曰阇婆，皆入貢。

translations.literal: In the Tang it was called Heling, also Shepo; its king resided in Zhepo city. The Song called it Zhepo; all paid tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times it was called Heling, also Shepo; its king lived in Zhepo city. The Song knew it as Zhepo. In each period it sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年，其王摩那駝喃遣使奉表，貢方物，其後不復 至。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongwu, its king Manatuonan sent envoys bearing a memorial and local products; afterward they never came again.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 11 its king Manatuonan sent envoys with a memorial and tribute goods, but afterward no further missions came.

sentences.zh: 或曰爪哇即阇婆。

translations.literal: Some say Java is Zhepo.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that Java and Zhepo were the same country.

sentences.zh: 然《元史爪哇傳》不言，且曰：「其風俗、物產無所考。

translations.literal: Yet the "Account of Java" in the History of Yuan says nothing of this, and states: "Its customs and products cannot be verified."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the History of Yuan's account of Java says nothing of this, and remarks, "Its customs and products cannot be verified."

sentences.zh: 」 太祖時，兩國並時入貢，其王之名不同。

translations.literal: In the Founder's time, the two countries simultaneously sent tribute, and the names of their kings were different.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongwu Emperor, the two states sent tribute at the same time, and their kings bore different names.

sentences.zh: 或本為二國，其後為爪哇所滅，然不可考。

translations.literal: Perhaps they were originally two states and afterward Java destroyed one; yet this cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps they had originally been two separate kingdoms and Java later destroyed one of them, but this cannot be confirmed.

sentences.zh: 蘇吉丹

translations.literal: Sukadana
translations.idiomatic: Sukadana

sentences.zh: 蘇吉丹，爪哇屬國，後訛為思吉港。

translations.literal: Sukadana, a dependency of Java, was later corrupted in name to Sijigang.
translations.idiomatic: Sukadana was a dependency of Java; later its name was garbled as Sijigang.

sentences.zh: 國在山中，止數聚落。

translations.literal: The state lies in the mountains, with only a few settlements.
translations.idiomatic: The country stood in the mountains and had only a few clustered settlements.

sentences.zh: 酋居吉力石。

translations.literal: The chieftain resides at Jilishí.
translations.idiomatic: Its chief lived at Jilishí.

sentences.zh: 其水 潏，舟不可泊。

translations.literal: The waters are swift; boats cannot anchor.
translations.idiomatic: The currents were rapid and ships could not moor there.

sentences.zh: 商船但往饒洞，其地平衍，國人皆就此貿易。

translations.literal: Merchant ships only go to Raodong—the ground there is flat, and all the people of the country trade there.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant vessels went only to Raodong, where the land was level and all the people of the country gathered to trade.

sentences.zh: 其與國有思魯瓦及豬 蠻。

translations.literal: Its neighboring states include Siluwa and Zhūmán.
translations.idiomatic: Its neighboring states included Siluwa and Zhūmán.

sentences.zh: 豬蠻多盜，華人鮮至。

translations.literal: Zhūmán has many bandits, and Chinese rarely go there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhūmán was rife with robbers, and Chinese seldom went there.

sentences.zh: 碟裡，近爪哇。

translations.literal: Deli, near Java.
translations.idiomatic: Deli lay near Java.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年遣使附其使臣來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle it sent envoys attached to Java's envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 it sent envoys attached to Java's mission to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 其地尚釋教，俗淳少訟，物產甚 薄。

translations.literal: The place honors Buddhism; its customs are simple and lawsuits are few; its products are very scarce.
translations.idiomatic: The people honored Buddhism, their customs were plain and litigation rare, and local products were very few.

sentences.zh: 日羅夏治

translations.literal: Jiluoxiazhi
translations.idiomatic: Jilochi

sentences.zh: 日羅夏治，近爪哇。

translations.literal: Jiluoxiazhi, near Java.
translations.idiomatic: Jilochi lay near Java.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年遣使附其使臣入貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle it sent envoys attached to Java's envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 it sent envoys attached to Java's mission to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 國小，知種藝，無盜賊。

translations.literal: The state is small; the people know agriculture and planting; there are no bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The state was small. The people understood farming and cultivation, and there were no thieves.

sentences.zh: 亦 尚釋教，所產止蘇木、胡椒。

translations.literal: They also honor Buddhism; what they produce is only sappanwood and pepper.
translations.idiomatic: They too honored Buddhism, and their products were limited to sappanwood and pepper.

sentences.zh: 三佛齊

translations.literal: Srivijaya
translations.idiomatic: Srivijaya

sentences.zh: 三佛齊，古名干陀利。

translations.literal: Srivijaya—in antiquity called Gantuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Srivijaya was known in antiquity as Gantuoli.

sentences.zh: 劉宋孝武帝時，常遣使奉貢。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu of Liu Song they frequently sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of the Liu Song it regularly sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝時數至。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Liang they came several times.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of the Liang it came several times.

sentences.zh: 宋名三佛 齊，修貢不絕。

translations.literal: The Song called it Srivijaya, and tribute missions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Song knew it as Srivijaya, and its tribute missions never lapsed.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，太祖遣行人趙述詔諭其國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, the Founding Emperor sent the envoy Zhao Shu to proclaim and instruct the country.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 the Hongwu Emperor sent the envoy Zhao Shu to announce the dynasty's accession to the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 明年，其王馬哈剌札八剌卜遣使奉金葉 表，隨入貢黑熊、火雞、孔雀、五色鸚鵡、諸香、苾布、兜羅被諸物。

translations.literal: The next year its king Maharajabaprabhu sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial, and together with tribute sent black bears, turkeys, peacocks, multicolored parrots, various incense, fine cotton cloth, Douluo quilts, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: The following year its king Maharajabaprabhu sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial, presenting black bears, turkeys, peacocks, multicolored parrots, assorted incense, fine cotton cloth, Douluo quilts, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 詔賜《大統 歷》及錦綺有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted the Datong Calendar and graded quantities of brocade silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted copies of the Datong Calendar and brocades and silks in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 戶部言其貨舶至泉州，宜徵稅，命勿徵。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue said their merchant ships had reached Quanzhou and taxes should be levied; the Emperor ordered that no tax be levied.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue argued that since their merchant ships had reached Quanzhou, duties ought to be collected, but the emperor ordered that no tax be imposed.

sentences.zh: 六年，王怛麻沙那阿者遣使朝貢，又一表賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, King Tammasanaze sent envoys to court with tribute and another memorial congratulating the New Year of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year King Tammasanaze sent envoys to court with tribute and a second memorial congratulating the coming New Year.

sentences.zh: 時其國有三王。

translations.literal: At that time the country had three kings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the kingdom had three kings.

sentences.zh: 七年， 王麻那哈寶林邦遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, King Manahabalimbang sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year King Manahabalimbang sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年正月復貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the first month, tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, in the first month, tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 九月，王僧伽烈宇蘭遣使，隨招諭拂菻 國朝使入貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Sanggaliyulan sent envoys who accompanied the envoys sent to summon and instruct Fulin to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month King Sanggaliyulan sent envoys who accompanied the Ming envoys dispatched to summon Fulin to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 九年，怛麻沙那阿者卒，子麻那者巫裡嗣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Tammasanaze died and his son Manazewuli succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Tammasanaze died, and his son Manazewuli succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使貢犀牛、黑熊、火雞、白 猴、紅緣鸚鵡、龜筒及丁香、米腦諸物。

translations.literal: The next year envoys were sent with tribute of rhinoceroses, black bears, turkeys, white monkeys, red-fringed parrots, tortoise shells, cloves, benzoin, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: The next year envoys brought rhinoceroses, black bears, turkeys, white monkeys, red-fringed parrots, tortoise shells, cloves, benzoin, and other goods as tribute.

sentences.zh: 使者言：「嗣子不敢擅立，請命於朝。

translations.literal: The envoy said: "The succeeding son dares not establish himself on his own authority and asks for orders from the court."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "The heir dares not take the throne without authorization and asks the court for its command."

sentences.zh: 」 天子嘉其義，命使臣齎印，敕封為三佛齊國王。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven commended this righteousness and ordered the court envoy to carry a seal and an edict investing him as King of Srivijaya.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this conduct and ordered the Ming envoy to carry a seal and an edict investing him as King of Srivijaya.

sentences.zh: 時爪哇強，已威服三佛齊而役屬之， 聞天朝封為國王與己埒，則大怒，遣人誘朝使邀殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Java was powerful and had already awe-subdued Srivijaya and made it a subject state; hearing that the Celestial Court had enfeoffed someone as king equal with itself, it was greatly enraged and sent men to lure the Ming envoy and kill him by ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Java was then strong and had already brought Srivijaya to heel and reduced it to vassal status. When it learned that the Ming court had enfeoffed a king of equal rank, it flew into a rage and sent men to lure the Ming envoy into an ambush and kill him.

sentences.zh: 天子亦不能問罪，其國益衰， 貢使遂絕。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven also could not demand punishment; the country declined further and tribute envoys ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not even demand redress. Srivijaya declined further, and tribute missions ceased altogether.

sentences.zh: 三十年，禮官以諸蕃久缺貢，奏聞。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, rites officials reported to the throne that the foreign lands had long failed to send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the Ministry of Rites reported that the foreign kingdoms had long stopped sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「洪武初，諸蕃貢使不絕。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In the early Hongwu period, tribute envoys from the foreign lands did not cease."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In the early Hongwu years, tribute envoys from the foreign kingdoms came without interruption."

sentences.zh: 邇者安 南、占城、真臘、暹羅、爪哇、大琉球、三佛齊、浡泥、彭亨、百花、蘇門答剌、 西洋等三十國，以胡惟庸作亂，三佛齊乃生間諜，紿我使臣至彼。

translations.literal: "Recently Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, Java, Great Ryukyu, Srivijaya, Brunei, Pahang, Baihua, Sumatra, the Western Ocean, and thirty other states—because Hu Weiyong rebelled, Srivijaya then nursed discord, deceived our envoys, and drew them to its territory."
translations.idiomatic: "Recently, among the thirty-odd states such as Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, Java, Great Ryukyu, Srivijaya, Brunei, Pahang, Baihua, Sumatra, and the Western Ocean, after Hu Weiyong's rebellion Srivijaya began sowing discord, luring our envoys to its shores and deceiving them."

sentences.zh: 爪哇王聞知，遣 人戒飭，禮送還朝。

translations.literal: When the King of Java heard of this, he sent men to admonish and restrain them and escorted them back to court with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When the king of Java learned of this, he sent men to rebuke the offenders and ceremoniously escorted the Ming envoys back to court.

sentences.zh: 由是商旅阻遏，諸國之意不通。

translations.literal: Because of this, merchant travel was blocked and the intentions of the various states could not reach us.
translations.idiomatic: After that, merchant traffic was obstructed and the goodwill of the various states no longer reached the court.

sentences.zh: 惟安南、占城、真臘、暹羅、 大琉球朝貢如故，大琉球且遣子弟入學。

translations.literal: Only Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, and Great Ryukyu continued tribute as before; Great Ryukyu even sent sons and younger brothers to study in the schools.
translations.idiomatic: Only Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, and Great Ryukyu kept sending tribute as before; Great Ryukyu even sent sons and younger brothers to study at the capital.

sentences.zh: 凡諸蕃國使臣來者，皆以禮待之。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys came from foreign states, they were all treated with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys arrived from foreign states, the court treated them with full ceremonial courtesy.

sentences.zh: 我視諸 國不薄，未知諸國心若何。

translations.literal: I have not been stingy toward the various states, yet I do not know what is in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I have never been sparing toward these kingdoms, yet I do not know what they truly feel.

sentences.zh: 今欲遣使爪哇，恐三佛齊中途沮之。

translations.literal: Now I wish to send envoys to Java, but I fear Srivijaya will obstruct them midway.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to send envoys to Java, but I fear Srivijaya may block them along the way.

sentences.zh: 聞三佛齊本爪哇屬 國，可述朕意，移咨暹羅，俾轉達爪哇。

translations.literal: I hear that Srivijaya was originally a dependency of Java; you may relay my intent and send a dispatch to Siam, so that Siam may forward it to Java.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Srivijaya was originally a dependency of Java. Relay my intent in a dispatch to Siam and have Siam pass it on to Java.

sentences.zh: 」於是部臣移牒曰：「自有天地以來，即 有君臣上下之分，中國四裔之防。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministry officials sent a dispatch saying: "Since heaven and earth have existed, there have been the distinctions of ruler and subject, superior and inferior, and the defenses between China and the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the ministry sent a dispatch stating, "Since heaven and earth came into being, there have always been distinctions between ruler and subject, superior and inferior, and defenses separating China from the four quarters beyond."

sentences.zh: 我朝混一之初，海外諸蕃，莫不來享。

translations.literal: At the beginning of our dynasty's unification, all the overseas foreign lands came to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: When our dynasty first unified the realm, every overseas kingdom came to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 豈意胡惟 庸謀亂，三佛齊遂生異心，紿我信使，肆行巧詐。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that Hu Weiyong plotted rebellion and Srivijaya then harbored a different heart, deceiving our envoys and acting with crafty fraud?
translations.idiomatic: Who could have expected that after Hu Weiyong's plot, Srivijaya would turn disloyal, trick our envoys, and resort to deceit?

sentences.zh: 我聖天子一以仁義待諸蕃，何諸 蕃敢背大恩，失君臣之禮。

translations.literal: Our sage Son of Heaven treats all foreign lands solely with benevolence and righteousness—why should any foreign land dare betray this great grace and violate the ritual of ruler and subject?
translations.idiomatic: Our sage emperor treats all foreign lands with benevolence and righteousness alone. Why should any kingdom dare betray such great favor and abandon the rites owed between ruler and subject?

sentences.zh: 倘天子震怒，遣一偏將將十萬之師，恭行天罰，易如覆 手，爾諸蕃何不思之甚。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven were aroused to anger and dispatched one partial general with a hundred thousand troops to reverently execute heaven's punishment, it would be as easy as turning over one's hand—why do you foreign lands not think more deeply?
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor were moved to anger and sent a single subordinate general with a hundred thousand men to carry out heaven's punishment, it would be as easy as turning one's hand over. Why do you foreign kingdoms not think harder about this?

sentences.zh: 我聖天子嘗曰：『安南、占城、真臘、暹羅、大琉球皆修 臣職，惟三佛齊梗我聲教。

translations.literal: Our sage Son of Heaven once said: "Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, and Great Ryukyu all maintain their duties as subjects; only Srivijaya obstructs our civilizing influence."
translations.idiomatic: Our sage emperor once said, "Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, and Great Ryukyu all fulfill their duties as subjects; only Srivijaya obstructs our civilizing influence."

sentences.zh: 彼以蕞爾之國，敢倔強不服，自取滅亡。

translations.literal: That puny little state dared to be stubborn and disobedient, bringing destruction upon itself.
translations.idiomatic: That tiny state dared to remain stubborn and defiant, and so brought ruin upon itself.

sentences.zh: 』爾暹羅恪守 臣節，天朝眷禮有加，可轉達爪哇，令以大義告諭三佛齊，誠能省愆從善，則禮待 如初。

translations.literal: You Siam have scrupulously kept your subject's conduct, and the Celestial Court has shown you added favor and ritual courtesy; you may relay this to Java and have Java proclaim the great principle to instruct Srivijaya—if they can truly repent their faults and follow what is good, they will be treated with ritual courtesy as before."
translations.idiomatic: You in Siam have faithfully kept your subject's duty, and the Celestial Court has shown you special favor. Relay this to Java and have Java proclaim the right course to Srivijaya. If Srivijaya truly repents and returns to the good, it will be treated with courtesy as before."

sentences.zh: 」時爪哇已破三佛齊，據其國，改其名曰舊港，三佛齊遂亡。

translations.literal: At that time Java had already destroyed Srivijaya, seized its territory, changed its name to Old Port, and Srivijaya perished.
translations.idiomatic: By then Java had already conquered Srivijaya, taken its territory, renamed it Old Port, and Srivijaya ceased to exist.

sentences.zh: 國中大亂，爪 哇亦不能盡有其地，華人流寓者往往起而據之。

translations.literal: Great turmoil arose in the country; Java also could not fully possess all the land, and Chinese who had settled there often rose up and seized territory.
translations.idiomatic: The region fell into great disorder. Java could not hold all the territory either, and Chinese settlers there often rose up and seized land for themselves.

sentences.zh: 有梁道明者，廣州南海縣人，久居 其國，『閩、粵軍民泛海從之者數千家，推道明為首，雄視一方。

translations.literal: There was one Liang Daoming, a man of Nanhai County in Guangzhou, who had long lived in the country: "Several thousand families of Fujian and Guangdong soldiers and civilians followed him across the sea; they made Daoming their head and dominated a region."
translations.idiomatic: One Liang Daoming, a native of Nanhai County in Guangzhou, had long lived there. Several thousand families of Fujian and Guangdong soldiers and civilians followed him across the sea, made him their leader, and he came to dominate the region.

sentences.zh: 會指揮孫鉉使海 外，遇其子，挾與俱來。

translations.literal: It happened that Commander Sun Xuan was sent on a mission overseas; he met Daoming's son and brought him back together with him.
translations.idiomatic: By chance Commander Sun Xuan was sent on an overseas mission, met Daoming's son, and brought him back with him.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年，成祖以行人譚勝受與道明同邑，命偕千戶楊信等齎敕招之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle, the Yongle Emperor, because the envoy Tan Shengshou was from the same district as Daoming, ordered him together with the company commander Yang Xin and others to carry an edict summoning Daoming.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 the Yongle Emperor, noting that the envoy Tan Shengshou came from the same district as Daoming, ordered him together with the company commander Yang Xin and others to carry an edict summoning Daoming to court.

sentences.zh: 道明及 其黨鄭伯可隨入朝，貢方物，受賜而還。

translations.literal: Daoming and his follower Zheng Boke accompanied them to court, offered local products, received gifts, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming and his associate Zheng Boke went to court with them, presented local products, received gifts, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，廣東大盜張璉作亂，官軍已報克獲。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiajing era, the great bandit of Guangdong, Zhang Lian, rose in revolt; the government troops had already reported his capture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiajing reign the great Guangdong bandit Zhang Lian rebelled, and the government army had already reported that he had been captured.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年商人詣舊港者，見璉列 肆為蕃舶長，漳、泉人多附之，猶中國市舶官雲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, merchants who went to Old Port saw Lian set up shop as chief of the foreign merchant ships; many people from Zhangzhou and Quanzhou attached themselves to him—it was like a Chinese superintendent of maritime trade.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 merchants who reached Old Port found Zhang Lian running a trading house as chief of the foreign merchant fleet. Many men from Zhangzhou and Quanzhou rallied to him, much like a Chinese superintendent of maritime trade.

sentences.zh: 其地為諸蕃要會，在爪哇之西，順風八晝夜可至。

translations.literal: The place is a key gathering point of the foreign lands, west of Java; with a fair wind one can reach it in eight days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: The place was a major meeting point of the foreign kingdoms, west of Java; with a fair wind the voyage took eight days and nights.

sentences.zh: 轄十五洲，土沃宜稼。

translations.literal: It governs fifteen districts; the soil is fertile and suited to crops.
translations.idiomatic: It governed fifteen districts. The soil was rich and well suited to farming.

sentences.zh: 語云： 「一年種穀，三年生金。

translations.literal: A saying goes: "Plant grain for one year, and for three years you produce gold."
translations.idiomatic: A local saying ran, "Plant grain for one year, and for three years you produce gold."

sentences.zh: 」言收穫盛而貿金多也。

translations.literal: This means the harvests are abundant and trade in gold is great.
translations.idiomatic: This meant that harvests were plentiful and trade brought in great quantities of gold.

sentences.zh: 俗富好淫。

translations.literal: The custom is wealth and lewdness.
translations.idiomatic: The people were wealthy and given to licentiousness.

sentences.zh: 習於水戰，鄰國畏之。

translations.literal: They are practiced in naval warfare, and neighboring states fear them.
translations.idiomatic: They were skilled in naval warfare, and neighboring states feared them.

sentences.zh: 地多水，惟部領陸居，庶民皆水居。

translations.literal: The land has much water; only the departmental chiefs live on land; common people all live on the water.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the land was water. Only the ranking officials lived on dry ground; ordinary people all lived on the water.

sentences.zh: 編筏築室，系之於樁。

translations.literal: They weave rafts and build dwellings, tying them to piles.
translations.idiomatic: They wove rafts, built houses on them, and moored them to piles.

sentences.zh: 水漲則筏浮，無沉溺患。

translations.literal: When the water rises the rafts float, and there is no risk of sinking.
translations.idiomatic: When the water rose the rafts floated with it, so there was no danger of sinking.

sentences.zh: 欲徙則拔樁去之，不費財力。

translations.literal: If they wish to move, they pull up the piles and go—no expense of labor or wealth.
translations.idiomatic: If they wished to move, they simply pulled up the piles and went, at little cost in labor or money.

sentences.zh: 下稱其上曰詹卑，猶國君也。

translations.literal: Subordinates call their superiors zhanbei—like a ruler of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates addressed their superiors as zhanbei, the equivalent of a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 後大酋所居，即號詹卑 國，改故都為舊港。

translations.literal: Where the great chieftain later resided was then called the State of Zhanbei; the former capital was renamed Old Port.
translations.idiomatic: The seat of the great chief later came to be called the State of Zhanbei, while the former capital was renamed Old Port.

sentences.zh: 初本富饒，自爪哇破滅，後漸致蕭索，商舶鮮至。

translations.literal: Originally it was very rich, but after Java destroyed it, it gradually declined, and merchant ships rarely came.
translations.idiomatic: It had once been very prosperous, but after Java's conquest it slowly withered, and merchant ships seldom called.

sentences.zh: 其他風俗、 物產，具詳《宋史》。

translations.literal: As for other customs and products, full details are given in the 《History of Song》.
translations.idiomatic: For its other customs and products, see the full account in the 《History of Song》.
